title: Star Trek: Picard
text: In 2399, retired Admiral Jean-Luc Picard lives on his family vineyard, haunted by Data's death and his failure to save the Romulans. A young woman, Dahj, who turns out to be an android with an organic body and a "daughter" of Data, seeks his help and is killed by Romulan agents. With the synthetic-life expert Dr. Agnes Jurati and a new crew, Picard searches for her twin, Soji, and their creator, Dr. Bruce Maddox, while the secret Romulan sect Zhat Vash hunts synthetic life; Jurati, manipulated by the sect, kills Maddox. Soji leads them to Coppelius, a hidden world of androids under Altan Inigo Soong, and Picard dies defending it before his mind is placed in a synthetic body. In the second season Q sends the crew back to 2024, where they meet Dr. Adam Soong and his synthetic daughter Kore. In the third, Picard learns he has a son, Jack Crusher, and reunites the old Enterprise crew against a Borg invasion. In the sources available, the series' biological science is the making of synthetic life. Dr. Bruce Maddox, a researcher at the Daystrom Institute, has built androids with organic bodies, Dahj and Soji, modelled on Data, and Altan Inigo Soong shelters a colony of such beings; both creators are presented sympathetically, and the villains are the Romulan Zhat Vash and their agents in Starfleet, who want to wipe synthetic life out. The second season adds Dr. Adam Soong, a 21st-century scientist and ancestor of the Soong family who has created a synthetic daughter, Kore, and whom Q uses against Picard's mission. The series asks whether synthetic beings, and Picard in his synthetic body, are persons. The sources do not describe the techniques used or any explicitly genetic storyline in the later seasons, so the genetic content of the series as a whole is not fully covered here.

title: Strain
text: This Nigerian drama, directed by Uduak-Obong Patrick, follows the Ezeji family after their six-year-old son Ekene is suddenly diagnosed with sickle cell disease. The diagnosis disrupts the family's life, and the parents, Nnamdi and Yemi, struggle to keep their peace and unity while dealing with doctors, a genetic counsellor, Ekene's school and the wider family, including his grandparents. The available source gives only this outline and does not describe how the story ends. The film won the award for best screenplay at The African Film Festival in 2021 and best international film at the Urban Film Festival in Miami. The film is about the impact of a genetic disease on a family. Sickle cell disease, an inherited blood disorder that is common in Nigeria and other parts of Africa, is diagnosed in the family's young son, and the story follows how the diagnosis strains the parents' relationship and family unity. The cast includes a doctor and a genetic counsellor, which suggests that the hereditary nature of the disease and its implications for the family are part of the story, but the available source does not describe what the counselling involves or how the story resolves. Sickle cell disease is a recessive condition: a child is affected when both parents carry the variant, which is why genetic counselling and carrier testing are recommended where the disease is common.

title: Superman: Red Son
text: In this alternate history, the infant Kal-El lands in a Ukrainian collective farm instead of Kansas and grows up to become the 'Soviet Superman', presented to the world by Stalin in 1955. President Eisenhower recruits America's best scientist, Lex Luthor, to counter him. After discovering that Stalin imprisoned his childhood friend Svetlana in a gulag, Superman kills the dictator and takes over the Soviet Union, ending wars and spreading communism, allied with Wonder Woman. Luthor unleashes a clone of Superman, grown from cells collected from a crashed satellite and powered remotely; to keep up in battle he overloads it until it dissolves, appalling Superman. Superman reprograms the alien Brainiac to help him rule, using its technology to lobotomize dissidents, and survives a trap set by a Russian Batman, who then kills himself. Luthor becomes US president and leads a Green Lantern corps against Superman. Superman, realizing he has become a tyrant, joins Luthor to defeat the treacherous Brainiac and disappears into ordinary life. Genetics appears in one episode of this Cold War superhero fable. Lex Luthor, America's top scientist, collects Superman's cells from a crashed satellite and creates a clone, the 'Superior Man', to fight him on the country's behalf; the clone is powered remotely, and when Luthor overloads it to keep up with Superman, it degenerates and dissolves into protoplasm. Superman, who is appalled, sees the clone as a living being sacrificed as a weapon, and the scene marks Luthor as ruthless in his early role as Superman's adversary, before he becomes a successful president who finally allies with Superman. The film's broader theme is the danger of absolute power on both sides of the Cold War rather than science as such; its other technologies, from red-sun lamps to Brainiac's lobotomies, are not genetic. Growing a full-grown superhuman clone from a few cells is comic-book fantasy.

title: The Old Guard
text: In this action film based on the comic by Greg Rucka, Andy leads a small team of immortal mercenaries, Booker, Joe and Nicky, who heal from any injury and have lived for centuries. A former CIA agent, James Copley, hires them to rescue kidnapped girls in South Sudan, but it is a trap: he films their deaths and regeneration. Meanwhile, the US Marine Nile Freeman survives a fatal wound in Afghanistan, and Andy brings her into the group. Copley has shown his footage to Steven Merrick, a young pharmaceutical executive, whose men capture Joe and Nicky and take them to his London laboratory, where they are tortured and sampled to uncover the secret of their healing. Booker, weary of immortality, betrays Andy, who discovers that she has become mortal. Copley, realising that Merrick is driven by greed and sadism, helps Nile rescue the team; Nile kills Merrick. The group exiles Booker for a hundred years, and Copley becomes their ally, showing them the good their missions have done. Genetics is a passing element. The immortals' healing is never explained, and the villain, the pharmaceutical executive Steven Merrick, wants to uncover its secret; according to the Italian source, he persuades Booker to betray the team by promising that their DNA could be exploited to find a cure for all ills. In practice, the research shown is the torture and tissue sampling of captives in a corporate laboratory, assisted by a scientist, and the film presents it as driven by greed and sadism, while the former CIA agent who first hoped to cure the world's diseases changes sides. The film is about immortality, loyalty and the exploitation of people by a pharmaceutical company rather than about genetic science.

title: The Stand
themes: engineered pathogens pandemic bioweapon post apocalyptic
text: In this miniseries adaptation of Stephen King's novel, a mishap at a top-secret military biological research facility releases a highly lethal strain of influenza, nicknamed Captain Trips, that kills nearly the whole population of the world. The survivors are drawn by dreams to two opposing figures: Mother Abagail, a 108-year-old woman who gathers the good in Boulder, Colorado, and the demonic Randall Flagg, the Dark Man, who builds a violent community in Las Vegas. Among the survivors are Stu Redman, Frannie Goldsmith, the deaf Nick Andros and the musician Larry Underwood, who join Boulder, while the resentful Harold Lauder and Nadine Cross go over to Flagg. As Flagg moves to destroy Mother Abagail's community, the story becomes an elemental struggle between good and evil, resolved in a final confrontation and a new closing episode written by Stephen King with his son Owen King. Genetics matters here only as the origin of the apocalypse. The plague is a lethal influenza strain held at a secret military biological research facility and released by accident, a mishap that kills about 99 percent of humanity; the sources do not say whether the strain was engineered or what the research was for, and they give no individual scientists a role beyond the opening episode. After the outbreak the series turns away from science altogether, towards a supernatural battle between good and evil embodied by Mother Abagail and Randall Flagg. As in the novel, military bioweapons research is the unexamined sin that ends the old world, presented through its consequences rather than through the people responsible.

title: The Superdeep
text: In 1984 the Soviet epidemiologist Anna Fedorova, wracked by guilt after a colleague died testing her vaccine on himself, is sent by GRU Colonel Morozov to the Kola Superdeep Borehole, where a secret laboratory lies deep beneath the permafrost. Strange sounds have been recorded underground, twenty people have vanished, and the site's head, Dr. Grigoriev, has concealed an outbreak; Anna's task is to bring back samples. With a squad of soldiers led by Major Mikheev, she descends into the facility, which Grigoriev tries to seal, and finds a fungal infection that covers its victims with mould and melts them into monstrous fused bodies. Anna learns that the fungus dies in the cold and needs warm hosts. Morozov refuses to call for rescue, intent on securing a biological weapon for the state, and the deputy head of research wants the discovery for his own fame. Most of the group dies; at the bottom Anna sees a vast glowing fungal colony. Infected, she escapes to the surface and primes a grenade to destroy herself and the fungus. The film is a Soviet-set body-horror story about a pathogen and the state's wish to weaponize it. The threat is a mould-like fungus found in the depths of the borehole, which infects warm-bodied hosts through spores and fuses them into mutated masses; the sources do not say it was engineered. What brings it into the genetics-adjacent category is the secret laboratory beneath the permafrost and Colonel Morozov, a military intelligence officer who sees the outbreak as a biological weapon for the state and puts everyone at risk to obtain it, while the deputy research head wants the glory of the discovery. Against them stands Anna, an epidemiologist presented as a responsible scientist, who in the end tries to sacrifice herself to keep the infection from reaching the surface. The film draws on the 'Well to Hell' legend of the real Kola borehole and on The Thing; its fungus is invented.

title: The Timeless Children
text: In the conclusion of a two-part story, the Master takes the Thirteenth Doctor to the ruins of Gallifrey and traps her in the Matrix, the Time Lords' repository of knowledge, to reveal their secret history. The explorer Tecteun found a child from another dimension who could regenerate, adopted and studied her, and grafted the ability into her own people, creating the Time Lords; that Timeless Child is the Doctor, whose earlier lives were erased from her memory after she served a secret organisation, the Division. Meanwhile, the Master seizes the Cyberium from the Cyber-Controller Ashad and uses it and the bodies of dead Time Lords to create regenerating CyberMasters. The Doctor's companions escape a Cyber-ship to Gallifrey. Encouraged by a past incarnation, the Doctor overloads the Matrix with her memories and escapes; Ko Sharmus detonates a Death Particle that destroys the Cybermen and Gallifrey, the Master escapes, and the Doctor is imprisoned by the Judoon. The episode rewrites the Time Lords' origins in biological terms. Tecteun, an explorer, studied a foundling child who could regenerate, subjected her to repeated forced regenerations, and grafted the ability into her own species, the Shobogans, turning them into the Time Lords, who then limited themselves to twelve regenerations. The Doctor is that child, so her genetics are the template for Time Lord society, a fact the Master resents because it means he was made from her. The Master in turn uses the Cyberium and the bodies of dead Time Lords to create CyberMasters, Cybermen that can regenerate. The revelation casts the Time Lords' defining trait as the product of experiments on a child, carried out by an ambitious scientist and covered up by the Division, and the Master as the villain who weaponises it. The genetics of regeneration is not explained; it is a narrative device of the series.

title: Tremors: Shrieker Island
text: The seventh Tremors film. Bill, a big-game hunter who owns the biotech company Avex-Bio Tech, takes wealthy clients to hunt Graboids, giant subterranean worms, on Dark Island, a private island next to a research station. When biologist Jasmine "Jas" Welker discovers a dead Graboid and its offspring, the Shriekers, which kill a colleague, she sends her assistant Jimmy to find the veteran monster hunter Burt Gummer, now living as a recluse. Jas learns that Bill has bred the Graboids to be stronger and more intelligent for his hunt and has cut off all communications. Burt reluctantly arrives, and with only old weapons from a World War II bunker the team fights the enhanced creatures, whose Shriekers can now use their screams as weapons. Bill refuses to stop the hunt and is eaten by the largest Graboid, "the Queen". Burt lures the Queen into a trap of spikes and dynamite, sacrificing himself to kill it. Genetic manipulation provides the premise of this monster film. Bill, the owner of a biotech company, has genetically bred Graboids to be more powerful and intelligent, purely to provide more challenging prey for himself and his wealthy hunting clients. The resulting creatures are superior to the originals of the series, and their offspring inherit the improvements, including Shriekers able to use sound as a weapon. The genetic engineer is presented as a reckless rich man who places his entertainment above other people's safety and is eventually killed by his creation, a familiar warning about tampering with nature for frivolous ends. Jas, a field biologist, represents responsible science and helps to stop him. The film offers no explanation of how the creatures were modified, and the genetics is a plot device rather than a subject. Its theme recalls Jurassic Park, with engineered animals bred for the amusement of the rich.

title: Trump vs the Illuminati
text: In 2044, artificially intelligent robots have drained the Earth of its resources, and humanity flees into space. A Chinese-made clone of Donald Trump, the 45th and 47th President, escapes from the maximum-security laboratory where he was held and stows away on the last shuttle off the planet. His craft crashes on Mars, where he is stranded alone for 999 years, joyriding in a Mars rover, while the rest of humanity wars with an evil alien race, the Illuminati. Learning that he is prophesied to destroy the Illuminati, the clone joins the surviving humans and takes the fight to the Illuminati's headquarters in Hell, where he must battle Satan himself. Genetics appears only through the premise of a cloned hero: the protagonist is a clone of Donald Trump, described as Chinese and kept in a maximum-security laboratory until he escapes. The film says nothing about who made him, how or why, and the cloning plays no further role in a plot driven by prophecy, aliens and a battle with Satan. This adult animated comedy, widely panned by critics as a low-effort far-right fantasy, uses cloning merely as a device to place its hero in the far future.

title: What Lies Below
text: Sixteen-year-old Libby Wells returns from summer camp to her family's lake house and meets her romance-novelist mother Michelle's new boyfriend, John Smith, an 'aquatic geneticist' who says he helps creatures adapt to changing environments and gives Libby a bracelet with fertility symbols. John behaves in increasingly predatory ways towards Libby, and she finds that he keeps parasites in the basement and walks into the glowing lake at night. Michelle, who has accepted his proposal, falls ill and finds she is pregnant; she refuses to believe Libby's accusations. In the basement Libby finds her mother in a water tank, giving birth to a dying creature, and her friend Marley's body being eaten by parasites. Captured, Libby sees several men identical to John and rows of women in tanks. John forces her to swallow a glowing substance, and she wakes in a filling tank, smiling as she discovers she can breathe underwater. The villain is introduced as an aquatic geneticist who claims to help creatures adapt to changing environments, and his real project is to breed a new aquatic form of life using human women: he marks them with fertility symbols, impregnates them, keeps them in water tanks and transforms them, while several identical copies of him suggest cloning or a hive. The film is a horror story about a predatory partner, and his scientific profession serves as a mask for sexual menace and bodily violation. The genetic mechanism is never explained (parasites and a glowing regurgitated substance play a role), and the ending, in which the heroine smiles as she breathes underwater, presents her transformation as a disturbing loss of self rather than a happy outcome. The science is pure fantasy.

title: Wife of a Spy
text: In Kiyoshi Kurosawa's historical drama, set in Kobe in 1940, the merchant Yūsaku Fukuhara lives a Westernised life with his wife, Satoko, and is warned by her childhood friend Taiji, now a military police officer, that he is being watched. After a business trip to Manchuria with his nephew Fumio, Yūsaku returns with a mysterious woman, who is later found murdered. Suspicious, Satoko learns the truth: in Manchuria the two men witnessed a secret Japanese army unit conducting biological experiments on civilians, including the deliberate spreading of plague, and they have obtained a doctor's notes and a film of the facilities, corpses and vivisections, which Yūsaku intends to make public abroad. Fumio is arrested and tortured. Satoko hides in a crate on a freighter with the film, but she is betrayed; the reel turns out to be one of Yūsaku's amateur films, since he swapped them. In 1945 Satoko is in a psychiatric hospital, and Yūsaku is reported lost at sea. The film's secret is a real wartime atrocity. The experiments that Yūsaku witnesses in Manchuria are those of the Japanese army's biological warfare programme, known historically as Unit 731, although the film does not name it: deliberate infection of civilians with plague, vivisection and the burning of bodies, documented in a doctor's notes and a film. The scientists never appear on screen; their work is presented only as evidence of a crime that the hero risks everything to reveal, and the story weighs national loyalty against the moral duty to expose it. The genetic element is thus limited to the pathogen used as a weapon, which places the film among stories of lab-held and weaponised diseases rather than of genetics proper. The film is fiction, but Unit 731 did carry out plague experiments on prisoners and civilians in occupied China.

title: Blue Heart
text: Miguel Coyula's experimental Cuban science fiction film, shot clandestinely over ten years, is set in an alternative history in which Fidel Castro oversees a genetic engineering programme to create the 'New Man' and save the Revolution. The experiments produce dangerous, unstable individuals who form an anarchist terrorist group threatening to destroy the society that created them, and who also become the target of a United States invasion under Donald Trump. The elliptical story follows Elena, one of these engineered people, on a journey toward the origin of her genetic code in search of her own humanity, alongside other characters such as David, Tomás, Diana and Fernando. The film mixes avant-garde and genre filmmaking and is loosely connected to Coyula's earlier Red Cockroaches. Genetic engineering is the film's central metaphor. The Cuban state, under Castro, turns to genetics to manufacture the 'New Man' of revolutionary ideology, and the result is unstable, violent people who turn against their creators. The programme is a political project of human improvement, close to eugenics, and the film presents it as the source of a dystopia; critics read it as a critique of states that depend on mythical figures and utopian promises, not only in Cuba. Elena's search for the origin of her genetic code is a search for her humanity, and critics noted that the film's heavy digital manipulation of images mirrors its theme of genetic manipulation. The sources describe the programme only in general terms, without scientists or methods; the idea of engineering political character through genes has no scientific basis.

title: Dune
text: In the distant future, the Emperor assigns Duke Leto Atreides control of the desert planet Arrakis, the only source of the spice, replacing House Harkonnen, but secretly plots with the Harkonnens to destroy him. Leto's concubine, Lady Jessica, belongs to the Bene Gesserit, a sisterhood running a centuries-long breeding programme; she was ordered to bear a daughter whose son would be the Kwisatz Haderach, a superbeing with prescience, but bore a son, Paul, instead. Paul, who has troubling visions of the future, passes the Reverend Mother's deadly gom jabbar test. On Arrakis, the Atreides are betrayed by their physician, Dr. Yueh, and the Harkonnens and the Emperor's Sardaukar attack; Leto is killed. Paul and Jessica escape into the desert, where they meet the Fremen led by Stilgar, including Chani, whom Paul has seen in his visions. Paul kills Jamis in a ritual duel and joins the Fremen. The film adapts the first half of Frank Herbert's 1965 novel. Heredity is a hidden engine of the story. The Bene Gesserit have spent generations arranging matings between noble bloodlines, with the aim of producing the Kwisatz Haderach, a man able to see the future and guide humanity. Paul is the unplanned result of Jessica's decision to bear a son, so he may be the expected superbeing a generation early, and his visions suggest that the programme has succeeded beyond its planners' control. The sisterhood is portrayed as a patient, manipulative political power that treats people as breeding stock, and the gom jabbar test shows how it measures "humanity" by its own standards. The breeding plan is a form of eugenics, a large-scale, long-term version of selective breeding, and the story's central fear, that a deliberately bred messiah may lead to holy war, is a warning about such projects. As with animal breeding, selection across generations can shift heritable traits, but nothing suggests it could produce prescience.

title: Emergency Declaration
text: At Incheon airport, Jin-seok, a strange young man, asks staff about popular flights, then implants a cylinder in his armpit and boards flight KI501 to Honolulu, which also carries Jae-hyuk, a former pilot traumatised by an emergency landing, and his sick daughter Soo-min. On the ground, Detective In-ho, whose wife is on the same flight, traces an online terror threat to Jin-seok and finds evidence of animal experiments and a decomposing corpse in his flat. Jin-seok releases a virus in the plane's toilet; passengers begin to bleed and die, and the captain succumbs, leaving Jae-hyuk and the co-pilot to fly the plane. In-ho learns that the virus is a mutated hemorrhagic virus linked to Jin-seok's dismissal from a pharmaceutical company. The United States, Japan and a fearful public refuse to let the plane land, and the passengers resign themselves to staying aloft, until an experimental antiviral drug proves effective and the plane lands at a military airstrip. A weaponised virus is the engine of this South Korean disaster film. The terrorist, a man dismissed by a pharmaceutical company, obtains a mutated hemorrhagic virus from the Middle East, tests it on animals in his flat and releases it on a transpacific flight, where it kills passengers within hours. The film says little about where the virus was developed, and its practitioners are the bioterrorist, presented as a sociopath, and the unnamed researchers whose experimental antiviral drug saves the survivors at the last moment. Much of the story is about the social response to contagion: countries close their airports, the public demands that the plane not land, and the passengers agree to sacrifice themselves. Released after the COVID-19 pandemic, it prompted one critic to ask whether a virus film was brave or sadistic at such a time. The speed at which the virus kills is far beyond that of real hemorrhagic fevers.

title: Evangelion: 3.0+1.0 Thrice Upon a Time
alt: シン・エヴァンゲリオン劇場版𝄇
text: In the final film of the Rebuild of Evangelion series, the WILLE organization restores Paris from the effects of an earlier catastrophe while fighting NERV's Evangelions. In the ruins of Japan, the despondent Shinji, Asuka and a copy of Rei reach Village-3, a survivor settlement where Shinji's childhood friends, now adults, help him recover; Rei learns to live among people but, cut off from the LCL fluid her body needs, dissolves. Shinji joins WILLE's attack on NERV in Antarctica, where his father Gendo seeks to bring about a final transformation of humanity in order to be reunited with his dead wife, Yui. Asuka learns she is one of a series of clones, and Gendo reveals that the Shikinami and Ayanami clones were made for the Human Instrumentality Project. Shinji confronts his father in a surreal space, comes to understand him, and chooses to remake the world without Evangelions. The film ends with an adult Shinji in a real, live-action world. Cloning is part of the mythology that the film resolves, although the story is about grief, maturity and letting go. Two of the young pilots are artificial: Rei is one of a series of Ayanami clones whose bodies need LCL fluid to hold together, and Asuka learns that she is one of the Shikinami clone series. Gendo Ikari reveals that both series were made for the Human Instrumentality Project, the conspiracy of the SEELE organization to force the next stage of human evolution, which Gendo pursues to be reunited with his wife. The clones are sympathetic characters whose artificial origin brings loss, as when Rei dissolves after finding a moment of happiness. Gendo is the antagonist but is treated with understanding in the end. The film never explains how the clones are made, and its idea of evolution is mystical rather than biological.

title: Foundation
text: Based on Isaac Asimov's novels, the series is set in the far future, when most of the galaxy is ruled by the Empire, a "genetic dynasty" of clones of the long-dead Emperor Cleon I. Three clones of different ages rule together: Brother Dawn, the young heir; Brother Day, the reigning emperor; and Brother Dusk, the retired elder. Unknown to the outside world, the dynasty has been guided for centuries by Demerzel, an ageless robot. The mathematician Hari Seldon has developed psychohistory, which predicts the behaviour of large populations, and he forecasts the inevitable fall of the Empire. With the help of the young prodigy Gaal Dornick, he persuades the Empire to let him establish a Foundation on the remote planet Terminus to preserve humanity's knowledge and soften the consequences of the fall. The series follows the conflicts between the Empire and the growing Foundation over the centuries. It premiered on Apple TV+ in 2021. Cloning is central to the Empire's storylines, and critics singled out the "genetic dynasty" as one of the show's highlights. The Empire's legitimacy rests on its rulers being exact copies of Cleon I, an attempt by one man to rule forever through his genome. The series uses this to explore whether identical genes produce identical people: the clones are raised to be the same, yet differ in temperament and choices. In the first season, Brother Dawn, who is colour-blind, turns out not to be an exact genetic copy of Cleon I and becomes involved with an anti-Empire plot to replace him with an impostor; the Cleons then learn that Cleon I's genetic code was meddled with and that Dawn is not the only clone with genetic abnormalities, undermining the dynasty's claim to purity. A religious leader who teaches that clones have no souls adds a further challenge. The scientists behind the cloning remain in the background, serving the throne. In reality, clones share their donor's genome but develop as separate individuals, as identical twins do.

title: Happiness
text: In a near future where epidemics have become the norm, a drug called Next, sold as a treatment that boosts strength and alertness, has started an outbreak of the Lytta virus, or mad person disease, which spreads through bites and scratches and causes white pupils, insatiable thirst and a craving for human blood. Police special forces officer Yoon Sae-bom is scratched by an infected trainee and taken to a research facility run by Lieutenant Colonel Han Tae-seok, where she appears to be immune. To get an apartment in a new, class-divided building, she enters a contract marriage with her old friend Jung Yi-hyun, a detective. When a resident who secretly bought Next turns, the building is sealed off; Sae-bom and Yi-hyun try to keep order among frightened, selfish neighbours, while Han, whose pregnant wife has been infected, wants to use the antibodies in Sae-bom's blood to find a cure. The series' epidemic has a man-made origin: the Lytta virus outbreak, or mad person disease, comes from Next, a drug made by a pharmaceutical company as a treatment for pneumonia and then promoted for boosting strength and alertness. The sources do not describe genetic engineering as such; the pathogen arises from a pharmaceutical product. The research side is embodied by Han Tae-seok, a military health officer who runs a facility where infected patients are held under observation, keeps the outbreak secret for as long as he can, and is ready to exploit Sae-bom, whose blood carries antibodies that might yield a cure, because he wants to save his infected pregnant wife. The series uses the epidemic to explore class discrimination and whether the infected remain human. A virus caused by a drug, and spread by bites with such symptoms, is fiction.

title: Invincible
text: Seventeen-year-old Mark Grayson is the son of Nolan Grayson, alias Omni-Man, the most powerful superhero on Earth and secretly an alien from the planet Viltrum. When Mark's inherited powers of strength, speed, near-invulnerability and flight appear, he becomes the superhero Invincible, juggling school, his relationships and his training. His world collapses when his father brutally murders the Guardians of the Globe, Earth's leading superhero team, and Mark learns that Nolan came to prepare Earth's conquest for the Viltrum Empire. Later seasons follow Mark's struggle to live up to and against his father, the threat of the Viltrumites, the multiverse villain Angstrom Levy, and a cast of heroes run by Cecil Stedman's Global Defense Agency. The family grows with Oliver, Mark's half-brother, born of Nolan and an alien woman on the planet Thraxa. The criminal Mauler Twins, experts in cloning, help the disfigured hero Robot move his mind into a clone of his friend Rex Splode. Heredity and hybridisation underpin this adult animated superhero series. Mark's powers are inherited from his Viltrumite father, and his half-brother Oliver, born of a Viltrumite and a Thraxan, combines traits from both parents, such as his mother's purple skin and his father's strength and slow ageing; inter-species offspring thus lie at the heart of the family drama, especially once Nolan's mission of conquest is revealed. Cloning appears through the Mauler Twins, criminals who reanimate a dead hero and clone Rex Splode so that the hero Robot, trapped in a deformed body, can transfer his mind into the copy. The available sources do not describe the Viltrumites' reproductive aims in detail, so the eugenic dimension of their empire is not covered here. Genetics in the series is comic-book biology, used to explore inheritance, identity and what children owe their parents.

title: No Time to Die
text: Five years after leaving MI6, James Bond is living in Jamaica when the CIA asks him to help find Valdo Obruchev, a scientist kidnapped from an MI6 laboratory together with Project Heracles, a bioweapon made of nanobots that can be programmed to kill people with a specific DNA. Bond discovers that Obruchev is secretly working for Lyutsifer Safin, who wants revenge on the criminal organisation SPECTRE and its leader Blofeld. At a SPECTRE gathering in Cuba, a mist of nanobots meant for Bond kills the SPECTRE members instead. Safin forces Bond's former lover Madeleine Swann to carry nanobots coded to kill Blofeld, and Bond, after touching her, transmits them to Blofeld, who dies. Safin then kidnaps Madeleine and her daughter, Mathilde, and plans to release the nanobots worldwide from his island factory. Bond destroys the factory but is infected with nanobots coded to Madeleine and Mathilde, so he can never touch them again, and he dies in a missile strike. The film's weapon, Project Heracles, is a form of genetically targeted killing: nanobots that spread by touch like a virus and kill only the person, or family, whose DNA they are coded to recognise. It was developed in secret by MI6 under M, so the threat originates in a government programme that creates a weapon of mass destruction, which is then stolen. Its scientist, Valdo Obruchev, is amoral: he secretly works for Safin and reprograms the nanobots for him, and Safin plans to distribute them worldwide. Genetics also shapes the ending: because the nanobots in Bond's body are coded to the DNA of Madeleine and her daughter, who is also his daughter, he can never touch them again, which gives his sacrifice its meaning. The heredity element is sound, since relatives share part of their DNA, but no technology exists that can recognise a person's genome and kill selectively in this way.

title: Oxygen
text: A woman wakes up trapped in an airtight medical cryogenic pod with no memory of who she is, while its oxygen supply runs out. The pod's artificial intelligence, M.I.L.O., will not open it without an administrator code. Contacting the outside world, she finds evidence that she is Elizabeth Hansen, a cryogenics researcher, and tries to reach her husband, Léo, but the voices she hears contradict one another. Eventually she learns that she is aboard a spacecraft, launched to carry thousands of people in hypersleep to a distant planet because a deadly virus is driving humanity to extinction. A video of an elderly Elizabeth reveals that she is a clone carrying the original woman's personality and memories; the woman she has been speaking to on Earth is the original herself. As the oxygen runs out, she disables the euthanasia protocol, reroutes oxygen from the pods of dead colonists and goes back to sleep. The clones of Elizabeth and Léo later arrive on their new world. Cloning is the film's final twist. The passengers of the colonial spaceship are clones of real people, carrying their memories and personalities so that humanity can survive a virus wiping out life on Earth, and the protagonist discovers that the person she believes herself to be is still alive on the planet. The film uses this to raise questions of identity and memory: whether a copy who remembers a life is the same person, and whether her love for Léo is her own. The scientist, the original Elizabeth, designed the programme to save the species and is presented sympathetically; the ethical problems of creating people for a mission are hinted at rather than explored. Cloning a human would produce a genetically identical baby, not an adult, and there is no known way to transfer memories or personality from one person to another, so the film's premise belongs to science fiction rather than to any real technology.

title: Resident Evil: Infinite Darkness
text: Set in 2006, between the games Resident Evil 4 and 5, this animated miniseries alternates between the present and flashbacks to a war in the fictional South Asian republic of Penamstan in 2000. Federal agent Leon S. Kennedy is called to the White House to investigate a hacking of secret presidential files. Claire Redfield, working for the NGO TerraSave on a refugee welfare project in Penamstan, is disturbed by a refugee child's drawing of what looks like a victim of a viral infection, and brings it to the White House, where she meets Leon; he dismisses any link. Soon the lights go out and zombies attack the White House. The two outbreaks, the war in Penamstan and the hack prove to be connected through a conspiracy over the creation and use of a virus, involving new characters such as Jason, a veteran of Penamstan, and Shen May. Leon and Claire uncover the scale of the threat and the immediate crises are resolved. The threat is a virus that turns people into zombies, and the series, described as biopunk, links outbreaks in a war zone and at the White House to a conspiracy behind the virus's creation and deployment, with critics noting its focus on geopolitical intrigue and corporate espionage. The available sources, however, give few details: they do not describe who made the virus, how, or for what purpose, nor the role of the scientist character, so the series' treatment of the science behind the outbreaks cannot be summarised more precisely from them.

title: Resident Evil: Welcome to Raccoon City
themes: engineered pathogens pandemic human experimentation mutants bioweapon
text: In the 1980s, Claire Redfield and her brother Chris live in the Raccoon City orphanage, where Claire befriends Lisa Trevor, a disfigured girl on whom Umbrella scientist Dr. William Birkin experiments. In 1998 Claire returns to warn Chris about Umbrella's experiments just as people begin to bleed, lose their hair and turn violent. Chris, Jill Valentine and Albert Wesker's police team are sent to the Spencer Mansion, where they find zombies devouring the missing Bravo team; Wesker is secretly working for another party to steal Birkin's virus. Claire and rookie officer Leon Kennedy flee the overrun police station, and Lisa leads them to a hidden laboratory where Umbrella experimented on children. Wesker kills Birkin's wife, Birkin injects himself with his G-virus and mutates, and Umbrella destroys the city. Leon kills the mutated Birkin, and the survivors escape with Birkin's daughter Sherry. This reboot of the Resident Evil film series, faithful to the first two video games, centres on the familiar picture of corporate bioweapon research. The pharmaceutical giant Umbrella has experimented on orphans in a secret laboratory under Raccoon City, and its research leaks into the town, turning the population into bleeding, violent zombies. Its scientist Dr. William Birkin has developed the G-virus, his life's work, which a rival party sends Wesker to steal; cornered, Birkin injects himself and mutates into a monster. The company responds to the outbreak by sealing the city, shooting those who try to leave and finally destroying it while reporting no survivors. Scientists and their employer are thus villains whose experiments on children and engineered viruses cause a catastrophe. The film does not dwell on the science, and the agents behave like no real virus.

title: Seobok
themes: cloning genetic engineering human experimentation human enhancement
text: Min Gi-heon, a former intelligence agent living in isolation and dying of a terminal brain tumour, is brought back for one last mission: to escort Seobok, the first human clone, created by the Seoin Research Institute through stem-cell cloning and genetic engineering. Seobok does not age and is effectively immortal, and Gi-heon is lured by the promise that research on him could cure his illness. As soon as the transfer begins, their convoy is attacked, and the two escape together. Seobok, who is seeing the outside world for the first time, asks Gi-heon to take him on a journey, and the two men, one who cannot die and one who is about to, clash and gradually bond. They are pursued by the company's chief executive, by double agents and by American agencies who want either to exploit Seobok's genetics or to eliminate him. Seobok's psychic powers grow, and in a destructive climax he kills the company's chief executive and fights off the military, until Gi-heon is forced to shoot him. Human cloning and genetic engineering are at the heart of the film. Seobok is a clone made from the DNA of a scientist's long-dead son and engineered to be immortal, so that his body can serve as a resource for prolonging the lives of others. The film presents the people around him as treating him as a laboratory asset rather than a person: the company, its wealthy backers and foreign intelligence services all want to control his genetics, while the scientist who made him keeps an emotional distance. Critics described it as a reflection on scientists playing God, in the tradition of Frankenstein, and on who deserves to live forever and at what cost; the contrast between the immortal clone and the dying agent drives the story. Human reproductive cloning has never been achieved, and a clone would simply be a genetic copy of the donor, with no inherent immortality.

title: Star Wars: The Bad Batch
themes: cloning mutants human experimentation human enhancement
text: This animated series, a sequel to The Clone Wars, follows Clone Force 99, the "Bad Batch", a squad of clone troopers whose genetic mutations set them apart from the rest of the clone army. When Order 66 turns the clones against their Jedi generals, the Batch's mutations let them resist, and they flee the new Galactic Empire together with Omega, a young girl who is an unaltered clone of Jango Fett, the template of all the clones. Over three seasons they work as mercenaries, lose their sniper Crosshair to Imperial reconditioning, and see the Empire destroy the cloning city on Kamino, replace clones with conscripted stormtroopers and turn cloning to new ends. The Empire's Advanced Science Division under Dr. Royce Hemlock experiments on clones and children for Project Necromancer, a secret plan to clone Emperor Palpatine. In the final season the Batch infiltrates the facility on Mount Tantiss to rescue Omega and other child test subjects. Cloning is the heart of the series. The clone army was grown on Kamino from the genes of Jango Fett, with modifications such as accelerated ageing; the Bad Batch are "defective" clones whose mutations give them enhanced senses, strength or intellect and, crucially, immunity to the programming that turned the clones on the Jedi, while Omega and the adult Emerie Karr are unmodified copies who age normally. The Kaminoan scientist Nala Se, complicit in the clone programme, protects the Batch and Omega in an effort to atone. The Empire treats the clones as disposable, kills off the programme and redirects cloning to Project Necromancer, in which Dr. Hemlock experiments on clones and on children with high "M-counts" to prepare a clone of Palpatine. The series sides with the clones as individuals, and presents cloning as a tool of states that use people as material.

title: Swan Song
text: In the near future, Cameron Turner, an artist, husband and father, is diagnosed with a terminal illness and keeps it from his wife Poppy, who is still grieving the death of her twin brother in an accident. Dr. Jo Scott, head of a high-tech cloning company working from a secret facility in the woods, offers him a way to spare his family: an exact double, designed to act and behave like him, that will replace him without anyone knowing and will not even know that it is not Cameron. Cameron goes to the facility, meets his replacement and befriends Kate, another terminally ill patient in the programme. Torn between protecting his family and the pain of being erased from their lives, and uncertain whether to tell Poppy, he wavers over whether to go through with the swap. The film was written and directed by Benjamin Cleary and released on Apple TV+ in December 2021. Cloning is the premise, but the film uses it to ask emotional and philosophical questions rather than to explore the science. The replacement is a physical duplicate of Cameron that behaves like him and believes it is him, an idea that goes well beyond biological cloning, which copies the genome but not a person's experiences or mind. The story focuses on grief, identity and consent: whether a loving deception is acceptable, whether the copy is the same person, and what the original loses by being replaced. Dr. Scott, the company's scientific leader, is presented as calm and businesslike, and some reviewers found her close to a villain, a provider of an ethically troubling service to the dying. In reality a human clone would be a genetic twin born as a baby, and nothing like this transfer of identity exists, so the film is best read as a meditation on mortality.

title: Sweet Tooth
text: Ten years after 'the Great Crumble', the collapse caused by a viral pandemic known as the Sick, babies born part human and part animal have appeared, and many people, unsure whether these hybrids caused the virus, fear and hunt them. Gus, a half-deer boy raised in hiding in Yellowstone by his father, Pubba, sets out after Pubba's death to find his mother in Colorado, protected by Tommy Jepperd, a former football player and reformed hybrid hunter. Their journey crosses other stories: Dr. Aditya Singh searches for a cure to save his infected wife under pressure from General Abbot, leader of the hybrid-hunting militia the Last Men, who has Singh's predecessor, Dr. Gladys Bell, poisoned; Bear leads an Animal Army protecting hybrids; and Aimee Eden runs a sanctuary for them. Gus learns that Pubba was a janitor at Fort Smith Labs and finally meets Birdie, a geneticist from the lab, who turns out to be his mother and had entrusted him to Pubba to keep him safe. Genetics enters through the hybrid children at the heart of the series and the laboratory behind its hero. Since the pandemic, babies are born with animal traits, deer, pig, fox, wolf or turtle, and nobody knows whether they are a cause or a consequence of the virus; the fear they provoke drives humans to hunt them, while others protect them in sanctuaries. Gus's story leads back to Fort Smith Labs in Colorado, where his father worked as a janitor and his mother, Birdie, as a geneticist; she gave Gus to Pubba to protect him. Meanwhile Dr. Singh's search for a cure is driven by love for his wife but carried out under the threat of the militia leader General Abbot. The sources do not explain how the hybrids or the virus arose, so the role of genetic research in the story is only partly documented here. The series, praised for its gentle tone, centres on kindness towards those who are different.

title: The Addams Family 2
themes: hybrids chimeras genetic engineering dna identification
text: In this animated sequel, Wednesday Addams presents a science-fair experiment in which she gives Uncle Fester the DNA of her pet octopus, and Fester slowly begins to change. Her work catches the eye of the scientist Cyrus Strange. Worried that his children are drifting away, Gomez takes the family on a road trip across the United States, pursued by a lawyer, Mr. Mustela, who claims that Wednesday was switched at birth and is not an Addams. Cyrus tells Wednesday that he is her real father, and a DNA test she runs with Gomez's hair seems to confirm it, so she leaves to join Cyrus in California. There he shows her his own formula for human-animal hybrids and reveals that his daughter Ophelia is a pig; he wants Wednesday's better formula and captures the Addamses to experiment on them. In the struggle Cyrus becomes a hybrid monster and admits he faked the DNA results. Fester, now an octopus creature, defeats him, and Wednesday restores Fester using the family's blood. Genetics drives both halves of the plot. Wednesday, a child prodigy of mad science, transfers octopus DNA into Uncle Fester to show how humans could be improved, and he gradually mutates into a tentacled creature before she restores him with the family's blood. Her rival is Cyrus Strange, a deranged scientist who makes human-animal hybrids, including his pig daughter Ophelia, and who wants Wednesday's superior formula; he ends up transformed by his own formula into a monster made of several animals. The other genetic thread is a paternity question: Cyrus fakes a DNA test to persuade Wednesday that he is her father, and the film, as some critics noted, raises the question of whether biology or love makes a family, answering firmly in favour of the Addamses. The science is cartoon fantasy: transferring an animal's DNA cannot turn a person into that animal.

title: The Silent Sea
alt: 고요의 바다 Mar de la tranquilidad
text: On a near-future Earth ravaged by desertification, drinking water is strictly rationed. A hand-picked team led by Captain Han Yun-jae, a space-agency soldier, is sent to the Moon to retrieve a mysterious sample from Balhae Station, a lunar research base abandoned five years earlier after an incident that killed all 117 people on board, whose circumstances were kept secret. The astrobiologist Song Ji-an joins the mission to learn the truth about the death of her sister, the station's chief researcher. At the station she discovers that their superiors have told the team half-truths and lies. The sample proves to be 'lunar water', a new substance that looks like water but multiplies like a virus when it comes into contact with living cells such as human blood. The crew are attacked by Luna 073, a violent superhuman girl who survived the incident and is immune to the lunar water, while some team members hide ulterior motives. The available sources describe the series' central biological element only in general terms. The sample kept at the lunar research station, 'lunar water', is a new substance that multiplies like a virus once it touches living cells, and its handling at the station caused the deaths of the entire staff, after which the authorities covered up the incident and sent a new crew without telling them the truth. Luna 073, the superhuman girl who survived and is immune to the substance, is the other mystery of the station, but the sources do not explain her origin or whether she resulted from experiments. The series thus frames the station's research as a secret, deadly project hidden by officials; the sources say nothing about genetic engineering or cloning, so any genetic dimension of the story cannot be confirmed from them.

title: Thunder Force
text: In 1983 cosmic rays give superpowers to sociopaths, who become supervillains called Miscreants; one of them kills the parents of Emily Stanton, both geneticists. Bullied at school, Emily is befriended by Lydia, who supports her dream of giving ordinary people powers to fight the Miscreants, but the two drift apart. In 2024 Emily runs a company continuing her parents' research. Visiting her, Lydia accidentally triggers a device that injects her with Emily's serum for super-strength, which requires a full course of treatments; Emily takes a pill version and becomes invisible. As the superhero team Thunder Force, they foil crimes, Lydia falls for a Miscreant called the Crab, and they refuse to work for mayoral candidate William Stevens, secretly the Miscreant King. When Stevens plans to bomb the new mayor's celebration, Emily's daughter Tracy injects herself with the serum to gain speed, and the trio defeats him; Lydia survives carrying the bomb into the river. Genetics is mentioned rather than explored in this superhero comedy. Emily's parents were geneticists researching a way to give ordinary people powers to fight the Miscreants, whose own abilities come from cosmic rays; Emily completes their work as a serum and pills that give strength, invisibility and speed. The sources never say how the treatment works, and the science is a quick device to create the heroines. Emily is presented as an obsessive but cautious scientist, the German Wikipedia noting that critics saw her as a dull mad-scientist stereotype; her research is ultimately a force for good, used to defeat the villain.

title: Triassic Hunt
text: Jordan Friedman, CEO of the Triassic Corporation, unveils his latest products: genetically modified predatory dinosaurs, highly intelligent and nearly invulnerable. Two Allosaurs being moved from a research centre to Los Angeles escape and hide in an industrial zone, killing a guard. Mercenary leader Luis, with Friedman's employees Dr. Elaine Kelso and Simone, sends his team into a warehouse to subdue the animals with tranquilliser darts before they reach a residential area, but the dinosaurs start hunting the hunters. The escape was no accident: Friedman released them deliberately and films the fight as a demonstration for buyers at an online auction of the creatures as super-soldiers. The mercenaries die one by one. The Allosaurs have laid an egg, and Kelso, determined to present her research, shoots Luis and Simone to protect it, before she is eaten. Joy lures the last Allosaur into an explosive trap, and Friedman meets his comeuppance. Genetic engineering creates the monsters and drives the plot. The Triassic Corporation, which develops biological weapons, has genetically modified dinosaurs to be intelligent, nearly invulnerable predators, and its CEO stages their escape so that their killing of mercenaries can serve as a sales demonstration for buyers who want them as super-soldiers. Its scientists are no better: Dr. Kelso is willing to murder colleagues to protect the dinosaurs' egg and get credit for her research. The film, a low-budget sequel to Triassic World from The Asylum, offers a crude critique of corporations that commercialise genetic engineering for military ends, and reviewers compare it to an economy-budget Jurassic Park. No scientific detail is given.

title: Y: The Last Man
alt: Y: The Last Man (serie de televisión)
text: This television adaptation of the comic book series begins when a mysterious event simultaneously kills every mammal with a Y chromosome, except Yorick Brown, an unemployed amateur escape artist, and his male capuchin monkey, Ampersand. With most of the US government dead, Yorick's mother, Congresswoman Jennifer Brown, becomes President and struggles to hold the country together while Kimberly Campbell Cunningham, daughter of the late president, challenges her legitimacy. Infrastructure such as the power grid and supply chains collapses, and social divisions persist. Protected by Agent 355 of the secret Culper Ring, Yorick sets out with Dr. Allison Mann, a geneticist specialising in human cloning, to find out what caused the plague and why he survived. The series also follows trans and intersex characters, as the die-off was defined by chromosomes, not gender. It was cancelled after one season with the mystery unresolved. The premise is genetic: whatever struck the world kills every mammal carrying a Y chromosome, so the series defines its victims by their karyotype. It takes care to separate chromosomes from gender: trans women and women with androgen insensitivity who carried a Y chromosome died, while trans men without one survived. The geneticist Dr. Allison Mann, an expert in human cloning, travels with Yorick to discover the origin of the plague and why he was spared, which implicitly raises the question of how the human species could continue. The available sources do not explain the cause, which the cancelled series never resolved, nor what Mann's research achieves. No known pathogen could selectively kill carriers of one chromosome across all mammals; the scenario is a thought experiment about a society without men.

title: Zombie Reddy
text: Game designer Mario travels with his friends Bhadram and Maggie to Kurnool for the wedding of his programmer Kalyan to Pushkala, daughter of the violent chieftain Bhooma Reddy, who is locked in a feud with the rival factionist Veera Reddy. On the way Mario runs over an infected man, who bites Bhadram, and a zombie outbreak spreads through the village during the wedding. Veera Reddy's men abduct Kalyan, and Mario sets out to rescue him with a wedding guest, Nandini, who turns out to be Veera Reddy's daughter Sailaja, and with Bhooma Reddy's henchman Kasi. Mario learns that the feud began when his own father jilted Veera Reddy's sister. Tracing the infection to a hidden lab, he meets a disgraced virologist who created the zombie virus by accident while trying to develop a COVID-19 vaccine, and who hints, before being killed, that the cure lies in a sacred temple. There Mario lures the horde into the temple's divine water, curing everyone, and the feuding families reconcile. The zombie outbreak comes from a laboratory: a disgraced virologist, working in a hidden lab, accidentally created the zombie virus while trying to develop a COVID-19 vaccine. The film, made during the COVID-19 pandemic and billed as the first Telugu zombie film, uses this as a satirical premise rather than a scientific one, and does not describe the virus in genetic terms. Science fails in the story: the well-meaning researcher unleashes the disaster and is killed by his first victim, and the cure comes not from medicine but from the divine water of a temple. Critics read the film as a satirical potpourri mixing pandemic, zombies and Rayalaseema faction rivalry.

title: A Cup of Coffee and New Shoes On
alt: Një filxhan kafe dhe këpucë të reja veshur
text: Agim and Gezim are inseparable deaf identical twins in their forties who live together in Tirana, work side by side in a carpentry workshop and spend their free time in a cabin in the mountains; Gezim's girlfriend, Ana, visits them regularly. Being deaf from birth has hardly limited their lives. One evening Agim's vision blurs while he is driving and he barely survives an accident. An ophthalmologist diagnoses both brothers with a rare, genetic, degenerative disease that will make them blind progressively and irreversibly, Agim first and Gezim later. As darkness closes in and the brothers face the prospect of losing their last means of communicating with the world and with each other, they make a grave decision together, over a cup of coffee and with new shoes on. The film is inspired by the real case of deaf twin brothers in Belgium who chose euthanasia in 2012 when they learned they would go blind. Genetics enters as fate. The brothers learn from an eye specialist that they share a rare, inherited degenerative disease that will make them blind, one after the other; the sources do not name it. Because they are deaf and communicate by sign language, blindness threatens to cut them off from the world and from each other, and the film focuses on their bond and on the decision they make, not on medicine. The diagnosis is presented factually, without villains or scientific drama, and no treatment is discussed. The film draws on the case of deaf twin brothers from Putte, Belgium, who were granted euthanasia in 2012 because of the unbearable prospect of blindness; the title alludes to the coffee and new shoes of their last day. Identical twins share their genome, so an inherited disease that strikes one will usually strike the other, which is precisely the situation the film dramatizes.

title: A Gaza Weekend
text: In this British-Palestinian comedy, co-written and directed by Basil Khalil, a catastrophic accident at an Israeli microbiological research institute releases a mutant virus, ARS, which spreads an epidemic across Israel. Because of Israel's blockade, Gaza ironically becomes the safest place to be. Michael, an Englishman, and his Israeli partner Keren try to flee the country, but their plan fails and they end up stranded in the Gaza Strip, where a local trader, Waheed, shelters them with his family. When the media report their presence, they are forced to devise a new escape plan. The film, conceived in 2009 and produced before the COVID-19 pandemic, won the FIPRESCI Prize at the Toronto International Film Festival. The premise is a laboratory accident: a mutant virus escapes from an Israeli institute for microbiological research and starts an epidemic. The virus is a satirical device rather than a subject; its main function is to turn the blockaded Gaza Strip into a refuge and the usual direction of flight upside down, which gives the film its political comedy. The researchers are never characterised, and the sources do not say whether the mutant virus was engineered or how the outbreak ends. Like many outbreak stories, it draws on public fears about pathogens escaping from research laboratories, though its concerns are the absurdities of borders and politics rather than science.

title: All of Us Are Dead
text: Based on a webtoon by Joo Dong-geun, this South Korean series follows a class of students at Hyosan High School when a zombie virus breaks out. Lee Byeong-chan, the school's science teacher and a former pharmaceutical researcher, created the "Jonas virus" to help his son Jin-su, who was being bullied, by removing his fear so that he could fight back. Instead, the injected Jin-su lost all his humanity and infected his mother, and Byeong-chan locked them up while he searched for a cure. An infected lab hamster bites a student, and the infection spreads through the school and the city of Hyosan, which the authorities eventually quarantine. Trapped in their classrooms, On-jo, Cheong-san, Nam-ra, Su-hyeok and their classmates fight to survive while the military and government struggle to contain the outbreak. Some of the infected keep their minds and become half-zombies. The series was renewed for a second season. The series is less about genetics than about biomedical experimentation gone wrong. Lee Byeong-chan, who holds a doctorate in cell biology, creates the virus in his school laboratory, reportedly from a hormone isolated from mice, with the aim of removing fear from his son; the result is a highly contagious agent that turns its hosts into rage-filled zombies. He is a tragic, morally compromised figure: a father who wanted to protect his child, who experiments on his own family and hides the consequences,. The series links his choice to the bullying and violence of the school, presenting the virus as an extreme answer to a social problem. No real virus could alter human emotions in this way, and the idea of "removing fear" with a single agent contradicts how complex behaviours are controlled by many genes, brain circuits and experiences.

title: Avatar: The Way of Water
text: Sixteen years after the Na'vi drove the humans of the RDA off Pandora, Jake Sully lives as chief of the Omatikaya with Neytiri, their children and their adopted daughter Kiri, mysteriously born from the inert avatar body of the late scientist Grace Augustine. They also look after Spider, the human son of Colonel Quaritch. The RDA returns to colonize Pandora, bringing recombinants, Na'vi bodies carrying the memories of dead soldiers, among them Quaritch himself, who hunts Jake for revenge. To protect the Omatikaya, the family takes refuge with the Metkayina, a sea clan, where the children are mocked for their human traits. Lo'ak befriends an outcast whale-like tulkun, and Kiri, linking to the sea's Spirit Tree, has a seizure. Quaritch joins a whaling ship and kills tulkun to draw Jake out, and the final battle costs the life of Jake's eldest son, Neteyam. The Metkayina adopt the family, and Jake resolves to fight. Genetic technology sits in the background of the Avatar story, and in this sequel it gives the villain his body. The avatars are engineered Na'vi bodies grown from human DNA, and the RDA now uses them to make recombinants, avatar bodies loaded with the memories of dead soldiers, so that Colonel Quaritch returns to hunt Jake. Heredity also plays a part: Jake's children with Neytiri have human traits, such as five fingers, which betray them to the RDA and make the sea clan's children mock them. Kiri, born from Grace Augustine's avatar body without any known father, is a mystery the film leaves open. The sympathetic human scientists, Norm Spellman and Max Patel, appear only to treat Kiri. Growing a hybrid body and transferring memories into it is science fiction; memories are not stored in DNA and cannot be copied into a new brain.

title: Black Crab
text: In a Sweden at war, former speed skater Caroline Edh was separated from her young daughter Vanja when the fighting began. Now a soldier, she is recruited by Colonel Raad for a mission called Black Crab: with a small team she must skate across the frozen Stockholm archipelago to deliver two secret canisters to the research base of Ödö, cargo that Raad says could win the war. She accepts because he promises that she will be reunited with Vanja. On the way, team members drown, are shot or turn on each other, and when they open the canisters they find vials marked as a biohazard, apparently a biological weapon; one of the dying soldiers shoots himself, warning that it would be the end of everything. Edh delivers the vials but learns that the promise about her daughter was a lie. She steals the vials back from the laboratory and destroys them with a grenade, dying in the act. The cargo at the centre of the mission is a biological weapon: vials marked with a biohazard warning, described as a virus or biological combat agent, that the military wants delivered to the Ödö research base, where scientists are to use it to win the war. The sources do not say whether it is engineered; it is a laboratory-held pathogen meant as a weapon of mass destruction. The military commanders, Colonel Raad and Admiral Nordh, are presented as cold manipulators who lie to soldiers to get the weapon delivered, and the base scientists remain in the background. As the soldiers realize what they are carrying, the film becomes a pacifist parable: one of them kills himself rather than serve it, and the heroine dies destroying it. Nothing is said about how the agent works.

title: Crimes of the Future
text: In an unspecified future, humans have undergone biological changes of unknown origin: most no longer feel pain or suffer infections, so surgery can be performed on conscious people, and some develop radical changes. Saul Tenser, who has "accelerated evolution syndrome", grows new organs, which his partner Caprice removes surgically in performances before an audience. The National Organ Registry, a government office that catalogues new organs to enforce limits on human evolution, takes an interest in them. Tenser also secretly informs for the police on a cell of radical evolutionists who have modified their digestive systems to eat plastic. Their leader, Lang, wants Tenser to perform a public autopsy of his son Brecken, who was born able to digest plastic and was killed by his mother. During the autopsy, the boy's organs turn out to have been replaced to hide the change, and Lang is murdered. Finally Tenser, struggling to eat, eats a plastic bar himself. The film is about human evolution and the control of the body, rather than genetics in a narrow sense. Humanity is changing in ways nobody fully understands, from the loss of pain to the spontaneous growth of new organs, and the state responds by cataloguing and suppressing these changes through a registry, while the evolutionists want to accelerate them and adapt human beings to a world full of plastic and synthetic chemicals. A boy born with the ability to digest plastic is the key evidence that the change is real, and the authorities destroy that evidence. Scientists appear only marginally: surgeons, bureaucrats and engineers of biomedical machines who are as invested in art and secrecy as in knowledge. As in much of David Cronenberg's work, biology is a metaphor for art, sexuality and our relationship with technology, and the film does not attempt a scientific explanation of its changes. Real human evolution happens over many generations through inherited genetic changes, not through the sudden appearance of new organs in individuals.

title: DC League of Super-Pets
text: In this animated comedy, Krypto, Superman's dog, fights crime in Metropolis with his owner but feels left out as Superman grows closer to Lois Lane. When the Justice League stops Lex Luthor from pulling an orange kryptonite meteor to Earth, a former LexCorp test subject, the guinea pig Lulu, grabs a fragment and gains telekinetic powers; the exposure also gives powers to animals at a shelter: Ace the dog, PB the pig, Merton the turtle and Chip the squirrel. Lulu captures Superman with green kryptonite, and Krypto loses his own powers after eating a shard. With the shelter pets, Krypto tries to stop Lulu, who empowers her own guinea pigs, captures the Justice League and frees Luthor, then turns against him. Krypto regains his powers, the pets rescue the League, and Lulu, after absorbing the kryptonite and becoming a giant monster, is defeated. The pets are adopted by the members of the Justice League. Genetics is a minor element. The villain, Lulu, is a guinea pig who was a test subject in Lex Luthor's laboratory, and one review describes her as genetically altered; her resentment of those experiments and her loyalty to Luthor drive her actions. The animals' superpowers, however, come from exposure to orange kryptonite, a fictional mineral, not from genetic engineering. The film is a family comedy about pets and adoption, and it does not explore the science.

title: Dragon Ball Super: Super Hero
alt: ドラゴンボール超 スーパーヒーロー
text: Commander Magenta, head of Red Pharmaceuticals, revives the Red Ribbon Army and recruits Dr. Hedo, the superhero-obsessed grandson of Dr. Gero, by persuading him that Capsule Corporation is an evil organisation. Hedo builds two androids, Gamma 1 and Gamma 2, and, from his grandfather's plans for Cell, the giant bio-android Cell Max. With Goku and Vegeta training on another planet, Piccolo infiltrates the Red Ribbon base and has a Dragon Ball wish unlock his potential. When Magenta plans to kidnap Gohan's daughter Pan, Piccolo stages the abduction himself to provoke Gohan, who overwhelms Gamma 1, while Piccolo convinces Gamma 2 that the Red Ribbon Army are the real villains. Magenta prematurely activates Cell Max and is killed by Hedo. The heroes and the Gammas fight the monster; Gamma 2 sacrifices himself, and Gohan, in a new 'Beast' form, destroys Cell Max. Hedo and Gamma 1 are given jobs at Capsule Corporation. Genetics is marginal. The villains' weapons are artificial beings created by Dr. Hedo: the androids Gamma 1 and Gamma 2 and the giant bio-android Cell Max, built from his grandfather's plans for Cell, a creature from earlier Dragon Ball stories. The sources describe them as androids and bio-androids without saying that genetic engineering is involved, and the story treats them as superhero action figures. The film presents their creation as dangerous in the hands of the Red Ribbon Army but redeemable, as the misled scientist Hedo turns against his employer and ends up working for Capsule Corporation.

title: Dual
text: In the near future, Sarah, a depressed alcoholic in a dull relationship, learns that she is terminally ill. To spare her boyfriend Peter and her overbearing mother the pain of losing her, she pays for a clone of herself, "Sarah's Double", who is to be trained to replace her after her death. The double soon develops her own personality and wins over Peter and Sarah's mother. When Sarah unexpectedly goes into remission and asks for the clone to be decommissioned, the double refuses, and by law the two must fight a publicised duel to the death a year later. Sarah trains with an instructor, Trent, and grows tougher. Shortly before the duel, the two Sarahs meet and agree to flee together, but the double poisons Sarah during a hike. Declared to be the original by a court, the double finds herself trapped in the same unhappy life, dominated by Peter and Sarah's mother, who both know the truth. Cloning is the premise of this deadpan satire, which imagines a society where people can commission an adult "double" to replace them after death, regulated by laws that require a duel when the original and the double both want to live. The cloning technology itself is never explained, and scientists hardly appear; the procedure is presented as an ordinary commercial service handled by clinics and the legal system. The film is less interested in genetics than in identity and worth: the double, genetically the same but shaped by different experiences, becomes a different person and is preferred by Sarah's family, while Sarah herself changes through training. It thus illustrates, in absurdist form, that sharing a genome does not make two people the same. Producing an adult clone ready to take over someone's life is not possible; a real clone would develop from an embryo and grow up over years.

title: Ghosts of Illyria
alt: Star Trek: Strange New Worlds, season 1, episode 3
themes: genetic discrimination genetic engineering human enhancement pandemic
text: The Enterprise investigates the disappearance of a colony of Illyrians, a people banned by the Federation because they practise genetic engineering on themselves. As an ion storm approaches, members of the away team return to the ship unknowingly infected with a virus that makes them crave light, and the infection spreads among the crew. Number One, the ship's first officer, is immune because she is secretly an Illyrian herself; she reveals this, but her blood holds no antibodies to make a cure from. The cure comes after her healing ability saves the infected security chief, La'An, from radiation, leaving antibodies in La'An's system that Nurse Chapel synthesises. Trapped on the planet, Pike and Spock discover that the colonists had been trying to reverse their genetic modifications in order to join the Federation, which left them vulnerable to the disease; they seem to have become the beings of light in the storm that protect the two officers. Afterwards Number One offers to resign, but Pike refuses. The virus reached the ship because Dr. M'Benga keeps his terminally ill daughter in stasis in a transporter. The episode is about prejudice against genetically modified people. The Illyrians genetically engineer themselves, which the Federation forbids, and Number One has hidden her Illyrian identity to serve in Starfleet. Her genetic difference saves the crew, although not by providing a cure from her blood: her healing ability rescues La'An, whose system then yields the antibodies for a cure. Yet she wonders whether Pike would have treated her differently had she not been useful. The colonists' attempt to undo their modifications in order to be accepted ends in disaster, presenting the ban as a source of suffering. The episode connects to the Star Trek tradition, rooted in the Eugenics Wars, of treating human genetic enhancement as dangerous, and questions it from the point of view of those excluded. No scientist is portrayed as a villain. Re-engineering adult humans in this way is far beyond current genetics, and the episode is interested in the ethics and politics of the ban rather than in the technique.

title: Halo
text: Set in the 26th century, the series follows humanity's war against the Covenant, an alliance of alien races bent on wiping it out. Master Chief John-117, a genetically engineered Spartan supersoldier, fights the Covenant on the colony of Madrigal with Captain Jacob Keyes and his daughter, scientist Miranda Keyes, and meets Kwan Ha, the teenage daughter of a rebel leader. John carries in his brain the AI Cortana, modelled on the brain of Dr. Catherine Halsey, creator of the Spartan programme, and forms a bond with Makee, a human raised by the Covenant's leaders. In the second season John and his Silver Team hunt the Covenant, meet the deserter Soren-066, contend with the Office of Naval Intelligence and face the invasion of the planet Reach, while more is revealed about Halsey, whose misanthropy drives her to 'improve' humanity by removing emotion. The series was cancelled after two seasons. Genetic enhancement defines the series' hero. Master Chief and his fellow Spartans are genetically engineered supersoldiers, products of the SPARTAN-II programme created for the military by Dr. Catherine Halsey; a newer SPARTAN-III programme recruits further soldiers in the second season. Halsey, the series' central scientist, is presented as brilliant but misanthropic: she believes emotion is the root of selfish behaviour and secretly aims to 'improve' humanity by removing it, she has made flash clones of herself, and she modelled the AI implanted in John's brain on her own. The Spartans are humanity's main defence against an alien genocide, yet the series dwells on what the programme took from them, notably John's attempt to recover his humanity. Real genetic engineering cannot produce supersoldiers; the idea belongs to military science fiction.

title: Jurassic World Dominion
themes: genetic engineering cloning de extinction gmo gene therapy
text: Four years after dinosaurs escaped into the wider world, they roam freely, and the company Biosyn Genetics runs a sanctuary in Italy's Dolomites where it conducts genomics research. Owen Grady and Claire Dearing secretly raise Maisie Lockwood, a teenage girl sought for her unique genetic makeup, until she and a baby raptor born by asexual reproduction are kidnapped and taken to Biosyn. Meanwhile, swarms of giant locusts are devastating U.S. crops but spare those grown from Biosyn seeds. Ellie Sattler and Alan Grant find that the locusts were engineered with Cretaceous and modern DNA and, with Ian Malcolm's help, go to Biosyn for proof. There the geneticist Henry Wu, forced by chief executive Lewis Dodgson to work on the locusts, reveals that Maisie is the clone of her mother Charlotte, who altered her DNA to spare her the fatal disease Charlotte herself suffered. The groups escape the burning facility, Dodgson is killed, Wu releases a locust carrying a pathogen that eradicates the swarms, and Biosyn Valley becomes an international sanctuary. Genetic engineering is everywhere in the film. Biosyn has engineered locusts with Cretaceous DNA that spare its own crops, so that it can control the world's food supply, an ecological crisis that director Colin Trevorrow developed after consulting scientists. Maisie is a human clone whose mother also edited her genome to prevent an inherited disease, and the cure for the locust plague comes from a custom-engineered pathogen, released by Henry Wu, that spreads through the swarm. The geneticists are divided: Dodgson is a corporate executive who exploits the science for profit, while Wu, a creator of dinosaurs in earlier films, now seeks redemption by undoing the damage. The film introduces feathered dinosaurs to the series, with the palaeontologist Jack Horner again advising, but its premise remains impossible: DNA degrades over time, and even under the best conditions samples older than about 0.4 to 1.5 million years do not retain enough of it for sequencing; claims of DNA from Cretaceous dinosaur bones in the 1990s may have stemmed from contamination.

title: Morbius
themes: genetic engineering hybrids chimeras genetic disease
text: Michael Morbius, a brilliant doctor who has suffered all his life from a rare blood disease, declines a Nobel Prize for his work on artificial blood.
