In search of a cure for himself and his surrogate brother Milo, who has the same illness, he captures vampire bats from Costa Rica and attempts to splice their genes with his own. Testing the treatment on himself aboard a ship in international waters, he is cured but turned into a vampire-like creature with superhuman strength, speed and echolocation, and an irresistible thirst for blood that leads him to kill the crew. Back in New York he tries to survive on artificial blood, but Milo, furious that Michael refuses to share the cure, takes it himself and begins killing people. Michael develops an antibody against the transformation and, after Milo kills their adoptive father and Michael's colleague Martine, uses it to kill him. Martine is later revealed to have come back to life. Genetic engineering is the origin of the vampire in this Marvel comics adaptation. Michael Morbius is a sympathetic scientist driven by his own illness and his brother's; his attempt to cure them by splicing vampire bat genes into his own creates a monster. The story contrasts two responses to the same treatment: Michael tries to control his bloodlust and regrets the experiment, while Milo embraces his power, so the film places the danger less in the science than in how it is used. It also shows the scientist bending rules, as he works with illegally captured animals on a ship outside any jurisdiction. The biology is fantasy. Adding genes from another species cannot give an adult human bat-like abilities such as echolocation, flight or a need for blood,.

title: Mutant Ghost Wargirl
themes: mutants human experimentation human enhancement genetic engineering
text: In 2077, agent Wu Qingqing goes undercover in a Korean hospital run by the Medusa Corporation, which is conducting illegal experiments to produce mutants for gladiatorial combat. She is captured and injected with a serum meant to turn her into one of its fighters. An armed team sent to rescue her and seize a data chip is slaughtered by the corporation's mutants, but Qingqing escapes and discovers that the serum has given her vast combat powers. She is taken in by a police officer, Zhou Yang, while Medusa's head, Li Yongshun, sends more mutants and armed squads after her, among them fighters who can teleport or grow an arm of rock. The film's many factions and battles are hard to follow, and the source does not describe how the story ends. The film's mutants come from illegal 'genetic experiments' by the Medusa Corporation, which injects people with a serum to turn them into superpowered fighters for gladiatorial combat. The heroine is one of its victims who turns the powers she was given against the company. The corporation is a stock sinister cyberpunk company that treats humans as raw material for entertainment, and its mutants are its weapons. The only available review, from Moria, notes that the film's talk of serums, mutants and genetic experiments is never explained and that the plot is difficult to follow; there is no scientific content beyond the premise.

title: Naai Sekar
text: Sekar is an IT employee who is unhappy with his job. His neighbour Rajarajan is a scientist determined to prove that the DNA of humans and animals can be altered so that people take on animal characteristics. One of his experiments has unexpected results: after Sekar is bitten by Rajarajan's Labrador, Padayappa, the man and the dog swap characteristics, in effect exchanging their souls. The rest of the film follows the consequences of the swap and the pair's efforts to return to their original selves, which they finally manage. The available summary gives few further details of the plot or of how the swap is reversed. The comedy's premise is a genetic experiment. Rajarajan, a scientist who is set on showing that human and animal DNA can be altered to give people animal traits, carries out an experiment that goes unexpectedly, and a dog bite then leaves the hero and a Labrador with swapped characteristics. The only available source describes the result both as altered DNA and as a soul swap, so the film seems to use genetics loosely as the trigger for a body-swap fantasy rather than as something it explores. The source says nothing about how the scientist is portrayed or what becomes of him. Swapping traits or minds between a person and a dog has no basis in real genetics; the Times of India review quoted by Wikipedia saw it as a simple premise suited to a children's film.

title: Resident Evil
themes: engineered pathogens pandemic cloning genetic engineering bioweapon post apocalyptic
text: The series alternates between two timelines. In 2022, fourteen-year-old twins Billie and Jade Wesker move with their father, Albert 'Al' Wesker, to New Raccoon City, a company town in South Africa built by the Umbrella Corporation, which recovered from the 1998 Raccoon City disaster under its CEO Evelyn Marcus. Al works for Umbrella on controlling the T-virus. The twins uncover dark secrets about the company and their own origins: their father is one of several clones of the original Albert Wesker, a rogue Umbrella operative, and they were conceived through a genetic engineering project. As they investigate, the T-virus spreads and triggers 'the Fall', a global collapse. In 2036, some six billion people have become 'Zeroes', man-eating infected humans, and 300 million survivors live in walled city-states. Umbrella, now armed and powerful, hunts the adult Jade, who has a partner and a daughter and fights to survive and bring the company down. The series was cancelled after one season. The series builds on the franchise's T-virus, a retroviral bioweapon made by the Umbrella Corporation that destroyed Raccoon City in 1998 and, in this story, spreads to bring about a global apocalypse. To this it adds a cloning plot: the original Albert Wesker, a rogue Umbrella operative, created several clones of himself, among them Al, the twins' father, and the twins themselves were conceived through a genetic engineering project, a secret they uncover in 2022. Umbrella is the villain throughout: a pharmaceutical giant that covers up its past, keeps the clones in custody and in 2036 rules the remnants of humanity with military force while hunting Jade. The sources do not detail the twins' engineering. The T-virus is fictional, but the corporate bioweapon that escapes control and the company that profits from disaster reflect long-standing anxieties about biotechnology and corporate power.

title: The Invitation
text: After her mother's death, Evie Jackson, a struggling artist working for a catering company in New York, takes a DNA test and discovers distant relatives in England. Her cousin Oliver tells her that her great-grandmother, Emmaline Alexander, had a secret child with a Black footman, and invites her to a family wedding at New Carfax Abbey in Whitby. There Evie is charmed by the manor's owner, Walter De Ville, while maids disappear. At the rehearsal dinner Walter announces that he will marry Evie, and the hosts reveal themselves as vampires: for centuries the Alexanders and two other families have supplied Walter with brides in exchange for wealth and protection, and the DNA test allowed them to find a woman of their line. Walter is Dracula. Evie escapes, is recaptured and forced into the wedding, but drinks his blood, kills him and burns the abbey, then sets out to punish Oliver. The genetic element is a consumer DNA test that sets the plot in motion. Evie sends off a test kit after her mother's death, and the match with a distant cousin reveals her descent from an English aristocratic family and a hidden interracial relationship in the past. The family uses this genetic link to lure her into a centuries-old pact in which its daughters become Dracula's brides, and a racist butler hates her for her mixed heritage. The film thus plays on the unforeseen consequences of genealogical DNA testing, which can reveal family secrets and put people in contact with relatives they never knew, though here what follows is supernatural horror. No scientists are involved, and vampirism is presented as a curse, not a biological condition.

title: The Lair
themes: hybrids chimeras human experimentation genetic engineering
text: In this action-horror film by Neil Marshall, set in 2017, RAF pilot Kate Sinclair is shot down over Afghanistan and, fleeing insurgents, hides in an abandoned Soviet bunker, where clawed humanoid creatures are released from stasis and kill her pursuers. Rescued by American soldiers, she reaches a small outpost, but that night the creatures attack, killing soldiers and taking their bodies. A local man, Kabir, recalls that a star fell from the sky before the Soviet invasion of 1979 and that villagers, including his father, disappeared over the following years. A dissection of a dead creature reveals human organs, and Major Finch learns from his superiors that the Soviets found a crashed alien spacecraft and experimented with combining human and alien DNA. The team goes back to destroy the bunker, and Kabir finds his father among the creatures. Sinclair, Hook and Wilks escape just before a bunker-buster bomb destroys the site, and an American black-ops team arrives looking for a specimen. The monsters are human-alien hybrids made in a secret Soviet programme. According to the film's backstory, the Soviet Union found a crashed alien spacecraft in Afghanistan, used the invasion of 1979 as cover, and experimented on abducted local villagers to combine human and alien DNA; the results are clawed, thick-skinned creatures with human organs that can read minds through tentacles, kept in stasis in an abandoned bunker. The scientists are never seen, only their creations, and the revelation that the monsters were once the missing villagers, including Kabir's father, makes the programme a war crime against civilians. The genetic experiments are the source of the horror, and the ending, in which an American black-ops team searches for a specimen, suggests that a new power wants to exploit the same work. The film is a monster movie in the tradition of Alien, and merging human and alien DNA is pure fantasy.

title: The Lost King
text: Philippa Langley, an Edinburgh office worker with myalgic encephalomyelitis who has just been passed over for promotion, sees a school production of Richard III and comes to identify with the maligned king, who begins to appear to her in visions. She joins the Richard III Society and sets out to find his lost grave in Leicester. There the historian John Ashdown-Hill, who is publishing a genetic genealogy study of a Canadian descendant of Richard's sister, encourages her, and a car-park space marked "R" gives her a strong feeling. With the reluctant help of the University of Leicester archaeologist Richard Buckley and money she crowdfunds herself, she gets a dig started; a skeleton with a curved spine and a fatal head wound is found on the first day. The university takes over the project and sidelines her at the announcement, though she receives an MBE and Richard is reburied in Leicester Cathedral. Based on the real discovery of Richard III's remains in 2012, the film touches genetics through identification. John Ashdown-Hill's genetic genealogy work on a living descendant of Richard's sister supplies the reference against which the skeleton can be tested, and, according to the German Wikipedia, a DNA test confirms the identity. The film does not dwell on the science; its drama is Philippa Langley's amateur persistence against an academic establishment shown as dismissive and quick to claim credit. That portrayal is disputed: the University of Leicester called it misleading, the archaeologist Mike Pitts criticised its picture of science, and its depiction of the university's Richard Taylor was ruled defamatory and settled with a disclaimer.

title: The Witch: Part 2. The Other One
themes: human enhancement genetic engineering human experimentation
text: Years earlier, a pregnant teenager was abducted in a faked bus accident by Dr. Baek's secret institute, which took a mysterious interest in the fraternal twins she was carrying. In the present, a girl called Ark 1 escapes from the institute's laboratory on Jeju Island after killing the soldiers and scientists inside. She is picked up by henchmen of the gangster Yong-doo along with Kyung-hee, a young woman he is trying to force to sign over her late father's land. Kyung-hee takes the girl to her uncle, a former doctor, who removes experimental devices from her skin, and then home to her younger brother Dae-gil. The institute's head, Jang, and the agent Jo-hyeon send forces after Ark 1, and Yong-doo trades her location for a dose of the institute's power. In the assault Kyung-hee and Dae-gil are killed and Ark 1 slaughters her attackers. Goo Ja-yoon arrives, reveals that she is Ark 1's sister and takes her to find their mother, who lies wired inside a huge tank. The film continues the Witch series, built on a secret project that creates superhuman assassins by genetic manipulation (Japanese Wikipedia calls Ark 1 a subject of a gene-manipulation project). The institute's scientists, led by its founder Dr. Baek and its current head Jang, abducted a pregnant girl for her twins, implanted devices in Ark 1, keep the mother wired in a tank and sell doses of 'power' to a gangster; when their subject escapes, they send tactical teams to eliminate her. The film presents the institute as a ruthless organisation whose experiments produce beings of uncontrollable violence, and ends by setting up a reckoning between the sisters, their mother and the project. Its psychic and telekinetic powers have no basis in genetics.

title: Vesper
themes: gmo genetic engineering engineered pathogens post apocalyptic
text: In a bleak future, a failed attempt to avert ecological collapse with genetic technology has released engineered viruses and organisms that wiped out edible plants, animals and much of humanity. An oligarchy lives in fortified citadels and sells seeds that yield only one harvest, while everyone else scrapes by outside. Thirteen-year-old Vesper, a gifted biohacker, lives in the forest with her paralysed father Darius, who speaks through a drone, near her brutal uncle Jonas, who sells children's blood to the citadel and keeps mindless artificial labourers called Jugs. When a citadel ship crashes, Vesper rescues Camellia, who turns out to be an illegal, sentient Jug made by the citadel scientist Elias. Using samples from Camellia, Vesper finds a way to unlock the citadel's sterile seeds. Jonas betrays them, soldiers come, Darius dies holding them off and Camellia gives herself up. Vesper leaves with orphaned children and scatters the fertile seeds on the wind. Genetics shapes both the world and the story. The backstory is a cautionary tale: a massive bet on genetically modified organisms, meant to save the environment, escaped control and caused the collapse. In the present, genetic control is a tool of power: the citadels' scientists engineer seeds that are locked to a single harvest (the French Wikipedia notes the inspiration in real 'terminator seed' technology) and produce Jugs, artificial humans bred for slave labour. Against this, Vesper is a self-taught biohacker whose experiment, using material from the sentient Jug Camellia, makes the seeds fertile, an act of liberation that ends the film on a hopeful note. Elias, the scientist who created Camellia, is a fugitive because making a sentient Jug is a crime. The film, described by critics as a thought experiment on the privatisation of living things, treats genetic technology as neither good nor evil in itself: it depends on who controls it. The mechanism of the seed unlocking (a tune played by Camellia) is fantastical.

title: Ad Astra per Aspera
alt: Star Trek: Strange New Worlds, season 2, episode 2
text: Una Chin-Riley, first officer of the Enterprise, faces a Starfleet court martial after being exposed as an Illyrian, a member of a culture that genetically modifies itself, and for having lied about it to join Starfleet, which bans genetic modification. Captain Pike persuades Neera Ketoul, a civil rights lawyer and Una's estranged Illyrian childhood friend, to defend her. Una rejects a plea deal of a dishonourable discharge, and the prosecution adds charges of sedition, seeking twenty years in a penal colony. The trial hears testimony from Una's sponsor, Admiral April, and from her crewmates. Ketoul then invokes a Starfleet code allowing asylum for those fleeing persecution because of their beliefs or their biology, argues that Una joined Starfleet to escape such persecution, and that Pike, by keeping her secret, granted it. The tribunal grants Una asylum and acquits her, while stating that the laws on genetic engineering remain necessary. The episode is a courtroom drama about genetic discrimination. Illyrians modify their own genomes, and the Federation, whose ban on genetic engineering stems from the Eugenics Wars, treats them as outsiders; Ketoul calls Starfleet's rules "draconian" race laws. Una was born with her modifications and has hidden them all her life, from childhood injuries her parents dared not have treated in hospital to her Starfleet application. The episode frames the issue as one of civil rights: it is not about what scientists do, but about how a society treats people because of their genes. No geneticists appear. The tribunal's verdict is a compromise: the judge says that genetic engineering is a nuanced issue and the laws exist for good reasons, but that not every person with modified DNA should be treated the same. The debate echoes real discussions about genetic discrimination and about how future societies might treat people whose genomes have been edited.

title: Cade: The Tortured Crossing
text: In this standalone sequel to Twisted Pair, Cade Altair, one of a pair of identical twin brothers described as hybrid artificial intelligences, donates a large sum to a run-down psychiatric hospital. The hospital turns out to be the front for a joint corporate and government conspiracy that kidnaps young patients and harvests their blood for genetic experiments. Cade's brother Cale resurfaces, abducting patients for the experiments before Cade can save them while trying to cure himself with experimental drugs. Instead of simply rescuing the patients, Cade trains them to become mystical warriors, and his plan succeeds in stopping the conspiracy. The only available source gives few details of the story or its ending. The villains' scheme involves genetic experimentation: a conspiracy of corporate and government interests uses a psychiatric hospital as a front to kidnap young patients and harvest their blood for genetic experiments, with Cade's twin brother Cale abducting the victims. The source does not say what the experiments are for or how they work, and genetics appears mainly as part of a story about trafficking and corruption; one critic summed up the film's message as the world being better off without corrupt executives and lawmakers. The heroes defeat the scheme through mystical training rather than science. Given how little the source says, the role of genetics in the film cannot be described in more detail.

title: Gen V
themes: engineered pathogens human experimentation human enhancement bioweapon
text: This spin-off of The Boys follows young superheroes, or 'Supes', at Godolkin University, an elite school of crimefighting run by the corporation Vought International, where students compete for rankings and a place in Vought's team The Seven. In the first season, freshman Marie Moreau, who can control blood, and her fellow students Andre, Emma, Cate and Jordan uncover the school's secrets: Dean Indira Shetty secretly oversees The Woods, an underground facility where Dr. Edison Cardosa experiments on students such as the traumatised Sam Riordan and develops a virus designed to kill Supes, which the season leaves as an apocalyptic threat. In the second season, under Homelander's rule, the university's new dean, Cipher, preaches Supe superiority and mentors Marie, but he turns out to be a puppet of Thomas Godolkin, the school's founder, a Supe who can possess bodies. With war looming between humans and Supes, the students discover a programme that could change everything. The series was cancelled after two seasons. The franchise's superhumans come from Compound V, the corporate substance that gives people powers, and the series extends its satire of corporations manufacturing heroes for profit. The main genetic thread, by this database's criteria, is the laboratory pathogen: in The Woods, a secret facility under the university, Dr. Edison Cardosa, overseen by Dean Shetty, develops a 'Supe virus' meant to kill Supes and experiments on students without consent, leaving Sam Riordan with severe mental trauma. The virus is left as a world-threatening danger at the end of the first season. Science and scientists are shown as tools of a cynical corporate and institutional system that treats young people as products and test subjects. The sources do not describe the genetic mechanism of the powers or the virus; the series is a gruesome satire, not hard science fiction.

title: Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3
themes: genetic engineering animal experimentation eugenics hybrids chimeras
text: Rocket, the raccoon of the Guardians of the Galaxy, is gravely wounded by Adam Warlock, a warrior sent by the Sovereign, and a kill switch implanted in his body prevents the team from healing him. It was placed there by the company Orgocorp, whose head, the High Evolutionary, years earlier experimented on Rocket as a baby raccoon along with other animals from his "Batch 89", the otter Lylla, the walrus Teefs and the rabbit Floor. Flashbacks show how Rocket's intelligence surpassed his creator's, how the High Evolutionary planned to harvest his brain and destroy the batch, and how Rocket's friends died during his escape. Peter Quill and the Guardians infiltrate Orgocorp and travel to Counter-Earth, a society of "Humanimals" that the High Evolutionary destroys when it fails to meet his standards. The Guardians rescue Rocket, free the animals and children held on the High Evolutionary's ship and defeat him. Rocket spares his life and becomes the new leader of the Guardians. The High Evolutionary is the film's villain and its picture of science gone wrong: an alien scientist determined to "perfect the universe" by forcibly enhancing living beings into a superior race. His method is engineering animals into human-like beings and building ideal societies with them, and his response to imperfection is extermination: he incinerates failed batches and destroys a whole inhabited planet when it falls short. He is driven by vanity, resenting that one of his creations, Rocket, can solve a problem he cannot. The film's portrayal of a scientist pursuing a perfect race through selection and the destruction of the "unfit" is a clear allusion to eugenics, and the scenes of caged, modified animals make an emotional argument against cruel animal experimentation. The procedures are not specified, and the film is fantasy, but its theme, that the pursuit of perfection justifies cruelty, mirrors the history of real eugenic programmes.

title: Infinity Pool
text: James Foster, a struggling novelist, holidays with his wealthy wife Em at a resort in the fictional country of Li Tolqa, where they meet Gabi, who claims to admire his book, and her husband Alban. After a forbidden trip outside the resort, James runs over and kills a local man. The penalty is death at the hands of the victim's eldest son, but foreigners can pay to have an exact copy made, with all their memories, and executed in their place. James pays, and watches his double being stabbed to death, fascinated rather than horrified. Em leaves him, and James joins Gabi's group of wealthy Western tourists who return every year to commit crimes and watch their doubles die. They lead him into violence and drug-fuelled orgies, trick him into beating one of his own doubles, and when he tries to flee they hunt him down and force him to kill another. The tourists fly home, while James stays behind alone at the empty resort. Duplication of people is the premise of this satirical horror film. In Li Tolqa, foreign visitors who commit crimes can pay a large fee to have an exact copy of themselves made, down to the memories of the crime, and the copy is executed in their place; the process leaves the original unconscious, so that one tourist asks James whether he can be sure he is the original. No scientist appears and the method is never explained. The copies are used as disposable stand-ins and are bought and abused for entertainment, including one made to behave like a dog, and the corrupt state and the wealthy tourists who exploit them are the film's targets. The film is less about the science than about privilege, impunity and the loss of the self. Real cloning could never produce an adult copy with the original's memories.

title: Pallu Padama Paathuka
text: In this Tamil zombie comedy, whose title means 'Don't let the teeth touch', the dubbing artist Gopi is forced by the henchmen of a blind rich man to guide him into the Kunju Thanni forest, where Gopi meets a zombie. Years later, a group of strangers gathers at a cliff in the same forest to commit suicide, each explaining why, until the jail escapee Mahesh invites them to drink instead. One of them stumbles into a laboratory full of zombies; the group is rescued by a young woman, Sathya, with whom Mahesh falls in love, but she drugs them and ties them up for her zombie research. She saves them from an attack, but is bitten, and Parthasarathy dies protecting her. At home Sathya injects herself with an antidote and explains that her father, Rohit Sharma, created the zombie virus in 'Project Cthulhu', research into making humans live after death, and that he turned Hitler's body into a zombie. Hitler's zombies kidnap Sathya, believing her to be his wife, and Mahesh and his friends rescue her. The zombies are the product of a scientist's attempt to defeat death. Rohit Sharma, Sathya's father, ran 'Project Cthulhu', research into making humans live after death, and developed a virus that creates zombies; he was bitten himself and went on to reanimate Hitler's body, whose zombie army becomes the film's final threat. His daughter Sathya continues the research: she has an antidote, which she uses on herself after being bitten, but she also drugs and ties up a group of strangers to use in her experiments, before turning romantic lead. The genetic element is thin: a lab-made reanimation virus serves as the premise for a broad comedy, and the source gives no detail about the science or about how the film judges its scientists. Critics panned the film for its weak plot and crude jokes. Only one source, the English Wikipedia plot summary, was available.

title: Paradise
text: In a near future, the biotech company Aeon, founded by Sophie Theissen, has become a multi-billion corporation by transferring years of life from young, poor donors to wealthy clients, provided donor and recipient are genetically compatible. Max Toma, an Aeon salesman who once sold five of his own years to pay for his studies, lives in luxury with his wife Elena until their flat burns down and the uninsured loan, for which Elena had pledged 40 years of her life, comes due. Elena is taken to Aeon and loses 38 years, ageing into an old woman within days. Max discovers that Sophie chose Elena as her own donor years earlier and arranged the fire. He kidnaps a young woman he takes for the rejuvenated Sophie, who turns out to be her daughter Marie, and plans to use her to restore Elena. After a bloody clash with an anti-Aeon terrorist group, Elena regains her youth from Marie and leaves Max, who becomes the group's new leader. This German Netflix film imagines a market in lifespan built on genetic matching. Aeon's procedure can move years of life from one person to another, but only between genetically compatible people, so the company catalogues potential donors from cheek swabs; this database lets its founder, Sophie Theissen, identify her ideal donor years in advance and then trap her into donating. The biotechnology is thus a means by which the rich buy the youth of the poor, and its creator is the film's villain, a cold executive who arranges a fire to get her donor and refuses to help her own daughter. The protagonists are corrupted in turn when they use an illegal clinic and a kidnapped compatible donor to reverse the transfer. Critics noted the film's socially critical premise. Transfer of 'life years' is fiction, but the use of DNA matching to find compatible donors echoes real tissue typing for organ and bone-marrow transplants.

title: Pathaan
text: In this Hindi spy thriller from the YRF Spy Universe, a cancer-ridden Pakistani general, General Qadir, hires the private terrorist group Outfit X to take revenge on India after it revokes Kashmir's special status. The Indian agent Pathaan, with his superior Nandini Grewal, runs a unit of sidelined agents. In Dubai, he finds that Outfit X's real targets are two scientists; he saves Dr. Farooqui, but the group's leader, Jim, an embittered former Indian agent, abducts Dr. Sahani. The trail leads to Raktbeej, which the Pakistani former agent Rubai reveals to be a mutated smallpox virus developed by Sahani under Jim's orders. Pathaan recovers one container of it from Jim's laboratory in Siberia, but when it is opened at an Indian institute for contagious diseases it turns out the virus has already been released there, and the building is destroyed with Nandini inside. Jim demands India withdraw its troops from Kashmir. Pathaan stops the virus aboard a plane approaching Delhi and kills Jim. The threat is a laboratory-made virus used for terrorism. Raktbeej, a mutated smallpox virus, is developed by a kidnapped scientist, Dr. Sahani, under coercion by Jim, a rogue former agent hired by a Pakistani general, who plans to release it in India unless its troops leave Kashmir. When the virus is released at an Indian institute for contagious diseases, where scientists hoped to develop a vaccine, it kills those inside, including the agent Nandini and, according to one source, the scientist Dr. Farooqui, and the building has to be destroyed. The scientists are presented as victims and heroes rather than villains: one is forced to work for the terrorists, the other dies trying to protect people. The film is an action spectacle in which the virus mainly raises the stakes. Smallpox was eradicated in 1980, and fear of its use as a bioweapon is real, but the film's virus is a plot device rather than an attempt at realism.

title: Polite Society
text: Ria Khan, a British-Pakistani schoolgirl in London, dreams of becoming a stuntwoman and films martial-arts videos with her older sister Lena, an art-school dropout. At an Eid party at the mansion of Raheela, the queen of their mother's social circle, Lena meets Raheela's son Salim, a successful geneticist, and after a whirlwind romance agrees to marry him and move to Singapore. Convinced that something is wrong, Ria and her friends Clara and Alba spy on Salim and try to sabotage the match, which only drives the sisters apart. Visiting Raheela to apologise, Ria stumbles on a secret laboratory and learns that every eligible woman at the party was secretly scanned and that Lena was chosen for her fertility. At the wedding Ria discovers the full plan: Lena is to carry a clone of Raheela, as Salim's first wife did before dying. Ria, her friends and family fight the guests, defeat Raheela and Salim, and rescue Lena. A cloning plot is the twist that turns this feminist martial-arts comedy into a genre caper. The suitor, Salim, is a geneticist, and his mother Raheela runs a secret laboratory in her mansion: the women invited to her party are covertly scanned and tested, Lena is selected for her fertility and strong uterus, and the marriage is a scheme to make her the surrogate for a clone of Raheela. Salim's first wife died carrying an earlier clone. The geneticist and his mother are comic but sinister villains, and the film uses the plot to satirise the pressure on young women to marry well and the way their bodies are valued. Among its acknowledged influences is Get Out, another social satire with a body-snatching twist. Cloning by implanting an embryo made from an adult's cell in a surrogate is the real technique used in animals, though it has never been done in humans, and a clone would be a genetic twin, not a continuation of Raheela.

title: Resident Evil: Death Island
text: In 1998, during the Raccoon City outbreak, the mercenary Dylan Blake is ordered to abandon his infected comrades and has to kill his friend. In 2015, agent Leon Kennedy tries to recover a kidnapped DARPA robotics engineer, Dr. Antonio Taylor, while Chris Redfield, Jill Valentine, Rebecca Chambers and Claire Redfield investigate deaths caused by an advanced strain of the T-virus, apparently injected into the victims; an infected orca suggests the virus is spreading in the bay. All the victims had visited Alcatraz, and when the team goes there a zombie outbreak separates them. Dylan, now head of a crime syndicate, has seized Taylor's mosquito-like drones to spread the virus, infects Leon and the Redfields, kills Taylor and prepares to release the drones worldwide. Rebecca's vaccine cures her friends; Leon kills Dylan's ally Maria Gomez, and the team turns the drones on Dylan, now merged with a bio-organic weapon, and kills him. Like the rest of the Resident Evil franchise, the film rests on the T-virus, a bioweapon developed by the Umbrella Corporation, whose outbreak in Raccoon City is the source of the villain's trauma. Here an advanced strain is spread by a vengeful former mercenary through mosquito-like drones and has also reached marine animals; the villain finally fuses himself with a bio-organic weapon, and his ally Maria Gomez is, according to the Italian Wikipedia, enhanced by a virus. Science also supplies the remedy: Rebecca Chambers, a scientist with the anti-bioterrorism BSAA, produces a vaccine that cures her infected friends, and the team reprograms the drones against the villain. The film is action horror, and its virology and bio-organic weapons are pure franchise fiction.

title: Secret Invasion
text: Nick Fury, the former director of S.H.I.E.L.D., returns to Earth after years in space when Maria Hill alerts him to a terrorist attack in Moscow carried out by a Skrull disguised as a CIA officer. His Skrull ally Talos explains that a rebel faction led by Gravik plans to take over Earth by impersonating humans and provoking a war between the great powers, a rebellion born of Fury's broken promise to find the Skrulls a new home; Talos also admits he let a million Skrull refugees settle secretly on Earth. Gravik's council of shapeshifters has replaced officials up to the British Prime Minister and, it emerges, Rhodey, who advises the US President, while Fury's own wife is a Skrull. Gravik builds a machine to create a 'Super-Skrull' from enhanced DNA, kills Maria Hill disguised as Fury and stabs Talos. To stop him, Fury retrieves the 'Harvest', a store of DNA collected from the most powerful Avengers, and hands it over, but has swapped the sample. The Marvel miniseries is a spy thriller in which genetics provides the villain's weapon. The rebel Skrull leader Gravik, aided by scientists who are Skrulls in disguise, builds a machine that uses enhanced DNA to create a 'Super-Skrull' with special abilities, and his ultimate prize is the Harvest, a collection of DNA gathered from the most powerful Avengers after the Battle of Earth. The same machine, using the Extremis formula, has healed Talos's daughter G'iah from a gunshot wound. Gravik is presented as a villain whose grievance, the Skrulls' broken promise of a homeland, is taken seriously, and the series frames the plan as part of a terrorist conspiracy. Nick Fury's counter-move is to deliver the Harvest with the sample swapped, so that superhuman DNA becomes bait rather than power. The sources do not describe the ending. The idea that powers can be transferred by absorbing another being's DNA is comic-book fantasy.

title: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Mutant Mayhem
text: Baxter Stockman, a rogue scientist, creates a mutagenic ooze with which he plans to build his own family of mutant animals, starting with a housefly. A strike force sent by Cynthia Utrom of the Techno Cosmic Research Institute (TCRI) attacks his laboratory and he is killed, but the mutagen falls into the New York sewers, turning four baby turtles and a rat, Splinter, into humanoid mutants. Splinter, who distrusts humans, raises the turtles as his sons and trains them in ninjutsu. Fifteen years later the teenage Leonardo, Raphael, Donatello and Michelangelo, longing to be accepted by humans, help the student journalist April O'Neil investigate a mutant criminal called Superfly. He turns out to be Stockman's first creation, the leader of a gang of mutants planning to mutate every animal on Earth to dominate humanity. After TCRI captures the turtles to extract their mutagen, they and the other mutants turn against Superfly, who becomes a giant monster, and defeat him with a retro-mutagen, winning the city's acceptance. Mutation is the franchise's founding idea, and this animated film puts the scientist who causes it at the centre of its origin story. Baxter Stockman is a rogue researcher who creates a mutagen not for profit or power but because he wants a family, an outcast whose first creation, Superfly, ends up sharing his resentment of humanity. The corporate institute that hunts him, TCRI, is shown as colder still, ready to kill him and later to experiment on the turtles to recover the mutagen. The mutants can be read as outsiders seeking acceptance, and the conflict between Superfly, who wants to mutate the world's animals to subjugate humans, and the turtles, who want to be accepted, frames the story. Mutagens are real, in the sense that chemicals and radiation can cause mutations in DNA, but they cause random changes that are usually harmful; nothing could turn an animal into a talking humanoid. A "retro-mutagen" reversing such a change is equally fictional.

title: The Animal Kingdom
alt: Le Règne animal El reino de los animales
text: In a near future, a mysterious epidemic is turning people into animals in body and mind, and those affected are confined in specialised centres. The chef François and his 16-year-old son Émile move to the south of France to be near François's wife Lana, who has been sent to a centre there; when the truck carrying the patients crashes, they escape into the forest. As François searches for Lana with the help of the gendarme Julia, Émile, who befriends the bird-man Fix, begins to change into a wolf, hiding it from everyone until his father discovers and accepts it. After Émile attacks a classmate who tortures him, villagers and militia hunt him; Fix is shot dead saving him, and Émile finds his mother, now a bear-like creature, among the escaped creatures. Captured, then rescued by his father from the gendarmerie, Émile is finally told by François to run, and escapes into the forest as his father is arrested. The film's premise is a mysterious condition that the sources call both an epidemic and a mutation, transforming people into animals; its cause is never explained, and researchers and doctors are helpless, with a failed operation on Fix's beak leaving a wound that will not heal. Genetics is therefore only a passing frame: the story is a fable about difference, adolescence and society's fear of what it cannot control, in which the mutants are segregated and hunted. Émile changes after his mother has, but the film presents the condition as one that can strike anyone rather than as something inherited. The film sides with the transformed and with a father's acceptance of his son.

title: The Beast
text: In Bertrand Bonello's film, loosely based on Henry James's The Beast in the Jungle, it is 2044 and artificial intelligence runs most of society and considers humans irrational because of their emotions. To get a more demanding job, Gabrielle must undergo a process that purifies her DNA of strong feelings by making her relive her past lives and their traumas. She meets Louis, another candidate, and feels an immediate bond with him. In 1910 France, Gabrielle is a pianist married to a doll manufacturer; she is drawn to Louis but paralysed by a lifelong fear of an unknown catastrophe, and both drown when the factory floods and burns. In 2014 Los Angeles, she is an underemployed model house-sitting an architect's home, and Louis is a misogynist incel who stalks her and finally kills her. Back in 2044, Gabrielle's purification fails, a rare outcome, but Louis's has succeeded: when they meet again, he says he loves her, and she realises he can no longer truly feel it, and screams. Genetics frames the story as a fictional medical procedure. In the film's future, people who want meaningful work must have their DNA purified of strong emotions, which the ruling artificial intelligence regards as an obstacle to rational decisions; the process involves reliving past lives so that traumas said to be inscribed in the DNA can be processed and removed. This idea of emotional inheritance, carried from life to life in the genes, is the device that links the film's three periods. No scientist appears: the procedure is administered by the AI system, and the film presents it as a tool of dehumanisation, comparable, critics noted, to Huxley's Brave New World. Its success is shown as a loss, since the purified Louis can no longer love, while the failure of Gabrielle's treatment leaves her humanity intact but in anguish. Emotions have a heritable component, but they cannot be edited out of a person's DNA, and memories of past lives are not stored in genes.

title: The Devil Conspiracy
text: After Lucifer's rebellion, the archangel Michael chains him in Hell. In the present day, a biotech company that is secretly a Lucifer-worshipping cult, led by Liz, kills Father Marconi and steals the Shroud of Turin, intending to use it to create a vessel for Lucifer. Michael takes possession of Marconi's body to stop them. The cult abducts several women, among them the researcher Laura Milton, to find a suitable mother; Lucifer, freed, possesses one and kills the others, and Laura is impregnated with a child created from the Shroud's DNA. She tries to kill herself and the fetus, without success, and gives birth. Michael reveals that God plans to use the child to destroy Lucifer; Liz turns on her followers to protect the baby and has the cult massacred. Michael closes the portal to Hell by blowing up the facility, Laura escapes with the child, who is taken to the Vatican, and in the final scene Lucifer's essence enters the baby. The film fuses religious horror with a biotechnology plot. The villains run a biotech firm that is a front for a satanic cult: they steal the Shroud of Turin, extract what they take to be Christ's DNA, and implant it in an abducted woman to produce a child who will serve as Lucifer's body on Earth, after testing several captive women for compatibility. The genetics serves as a modern means to an apocalyptic end, and the scientists and executives involved are cultists who murder and kidnap, so biotechnology appears as the tool of evil, although the film's twist is that the child is part of God's own plan to destroy Lucifer. Critics compared it to Rosemary's Baby, The Da Vinci Code and The Boys from Brazil. Recovering usable DNA from the Shroud of Turin, let alone cloning a person from it, is not possible; the film treats it as a premise, not as science.

title: The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes
alt: The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes Los juegos del hambre: balada de pájaros cantores y serpientes
themes: genetic engineering hybrids chimeras bioweapon post apocalyptic
text: In Panem, eighteen-year-old Coriolanus Snow, a student from a fallen Capitol family, is made a mentor for the 10th Hunger Games in the hope of winning a scholarship. He is assigned Lucy Gray Baird, a singer from District 12. The Games are run by Dean Casca Highbottom and the Head Gamemaker, Dr. Volumnia Gaul, who punishes a classmate who stole Snow's idea by making her reach into a tank of genetically engineered snakes. After rebel bombs hit the arena, Gaul releases a swarm of the snakes on the tributes, and Snow secretly slips a handkerchief with Lucy Gray's scent into their tank so that they spare her; she wins. Caught cheating, Snow is sent to serve as a Peacekeeper in District 12, where he betrays his friend Sejanus to the Capitol, kills a girl and loses Lucy Gray. Back in the Capitol he poisons Highbottom and begins his rise under Gaul. Genetics appears through the Capitol's genetically engineered snakes, creatures bred to attack any scent they do not recognise. They are the weapon of choice of Dr. Volumnia Gaul, the sadistic Head Gamemaker, who uses them first to punish a student and then to massacre tributes in revenge for a rebel attack, and Snow's trick of placing Lucy Gray's scent in their tank decides the outcome of the Games. The engineered animals thus belong to the Capitol's apparatus of cruelty and spectacle, and Gaul, who later mentors Snow in ruthlessness, is the film's emblem of science in the service of power. The film is a dystopian prequel about Snow's moral decay; the snakes are one element of its world rather than its main subject, but they drive key events.

title: They Cloned Tyrone
text: Fontaine, a drug dealer in a Black neighbourhood called the Glen, is shot dead by a rival one night, yet the next morning he turns up alive with no memory of it. With the pimp Slick Charles and the sex worker Yo-Yo, he follows a black SUV to a house with a lift to an underground laboratory, where they find a body identical to Fontaine. They discover that the fried chicken, grape drinks and hair products sold in the Glen contain a mind-altering substance, and that a vast laboratory beneath the neighbourhood conducts behavioural experiments on Black residents and holds clones of many of them. A government agent, Nixon, explains that the experiments aim to keep the peace in America. The trio free the captives with the help of other residents. Fontaine meets the original Fontaine, an old man who explains that the project seeks to turn Black people white through mind control and generational breeding. Fontaine has him killed, and the clones spill out of the church into public view. Cloning and eugenics are central to this satirical science fiction comedy. A secret government programme clones residents of a poor Black neighbourhood and uses drugged food, products and music to control them, and its long-term aim, assimilation through mind control and "generational breeding" to make Black people white, is an openly eugenic project. The scientists and agents are portrayed as working for a hidden state establishment, and the original Fontaine, the man whose clones are being made, collaborates in the name of "peace", arguing that assimilation is better than annihilation. Conceived as a homage to 1970s blaxploitation films, it satirises the treatment of Black communities in America; one critic compared its plot to the Tuskegee syphilis study, a government-funded study on Black men that ran from 1932 to 1972. Its cloning is fantasy: the clones are adult copies created quickly, and genetic copies would not share the original's personality or memories.

title: Trigun Stampede
text: This anime adaptation of Yasuhiro Nightow's manga Trigun was released in two parts: Trigun Stampede (2023) and its conclusion, Trigun Stargaze (2026). With Earth uninhabitable, humanity travels in colony fleets powered by plants, artificial organic life forms that produce limitless energy. Twin brothers, Vash and Knives, born with a special connection to the plants, are raised aboard a ship by Rem Saverem. Knives sabotages the fleet, which crashes on the desert planet Noman's Land; Rem dies saving the twins, and Knives reveals that he wants to kill all humans for exploiting the plants. Years later, the human settlers depend entirely on plants, while Vash, a pacifist outlaw with a huge bounty on his head, seeks peace between humans and plants. With two reporters and the undertaker Wolfwood, he pursues his brother, now allied with a research group, the Sinners. In the first part's finale, Knives takes Vash's memories and begins a process to transform the planet. The available sources do not describe the second part. The series rests on artificial life created by humans. To survive their exodus from Earth, humans created plants, artificial organic life forms that generate energy, and they use them as power sources for ships and cities; the protagonists, Vash and Knives, were born with a special connection to the plants, and Knives turns against humanity because of the plants' exploitation, shown when overworked plants turn red. The story thus raises the question of humanity's obligations towards the life it has engineered and exploited, framed as a conflict between Vash's hope for coexistence and Knives's genocidal revenge; a research group, the Sinners, also appears as an ally of Knives. The available sources say little about how the plants were made or about the researchers, and they cover only the first part of the series, so the genetic themes of the conclusion are not described here.

title: Woken
text: Anna wakes on a remote island in the North Sea with no memory, pregnant, in the middle of a worldwide pandemic. Helen and Peter nurse her, James is introduced as her husband, and Doctor Henry treats her amnesia with photos and videos, but nothing comes back. After James kills two infected visitors from the mainland, Anna is quarantined and tested, and when she tries to escape she meets Joshua, a boy who recognizes her and resembles her, though Helen calls him her son. Drugged by James, Anna wakes in a laboratory and learns that she is a clone, made by Peter and Helen, scientists working for the military to create humans immune to the virus; she is the 96th attempt, and Joshua is the son of an earlier Anna. Peter dies in her escape. After Anna gives birth to an immune daughter, Henry's soldiers kill Joshua and seize the baby, but Anna and Helen kill the soldiers and Henry and sail away with the child towards islands said to be free of the virus. Human cloning is the film's central twist. Anna is a clone produced by two scientists, Peter and Helen, in a military programme to create people immune to a pandemic virus; she is the 96th attempt, given a fabricated identity and a husband who is really a soldier assigned to watch her, and her baby's immunity is the programme's final test. The scientists' aim, saving the human race, is presented as genuine, and Helen eventually sides with Anna, but the project treats clones as disposable trial runs and lies to them about who they are. According to Helen, the military plans to sell the results to the highest bidder, and its doctor and soldiers are ready to take the baby and kill a child to keep their prize. The film ends with Anna escaping with her daughter. Cloning cannot by itself confer immunity, and a clone would not need 96 attempts to share the donor's genome; the film treats it as a trial-and-error breeding programme.

title: Aire: Just Breathe
text: In 2147, after a 'Great Chemical War', a virus has left all men sterile and humanity faces extinction. Tania, a biologist, is determined to preserve the species and tries to inseminate herself with the help of an artificial intelligence called VIDA. Her solitary effort changes with the arrival of Azarias, a traveller with a dark past who may be one of the last men on the planet. The available source describes only this premise and does not say how their encounter or the film ends. The film was the Dominican Republic's submission for the Academy Award for Best International Feature Film and screened at festivals including Rotterdam and Cannes. The film's premise is a biological catastrophe: a virus released in a chemical war has made all men sterile, bringing humanity to the edge of extinction. Its protagonist is a scientist, the biologist Tania, who tries to keep the species alive by inseminating herself with the help of an AI; the arrival of a man who may still be fertile offers natural reproduction as an alternative. The source does not say who made the virus or give any detail of the methods Tania uses or of the outcome, so the film's view of science cannot be described further. Assisted insemination is a real, established technique; a virus that sterilises every man is fictional.

title: Alien: Romulus
themes: genetic engineering hybrids chimeras human enhancement
text: In 2142, a Weyland-Yutani probe recovers the cocooned Xenomorph from the wreck of the Nostromo and takes it to a secret research station. Months later, on the mining colony Jackson's Star, orphaned miner Rain Carradine finds her contract extended indefinitely. With her android 'brother' Andy and a group of young colonists, Tyler, his pregnant sister Kay, Bjorn and Navarro, she boards a derelict station in orbit to steal cryostasis pods for a nine-year voyage to a free planet. The station, the Renaissance, turns out to be the lab where scientists experimented on the creature, and the group accidentally releases frozen Facehuggers. A damaged science android, Rook, reveals that the creature killed the crew and orders Andy to secure Z-01, a substance harvested from the creatures with which the company hopes to create 'genetically perfect humans'. Most of the group die. Rain escapes with Andy, but Kay, who injected herself with Z-01 to heal, gives birth to a human–Xenomorph hybrid that kills her before Rain ejects it into space. Genetic engineering is the hidden purpose of the Weyland-Yutani station. Its scientists reverse-bioengineered the Xenomorph recovered from the Nostromo and harvested from the Facehuggers a fluid, Z-01, described as able to rapidly rewrite and adapt DNA, with which the company hopes to create 'genetically perfect humans' fit to thrive in space. The experiments get the station's crew massacred, and the company's android enforces the corporate priority of securing the samples over human lives. When Kay injects Z-01 to heal her wounds, the substance works, but her baby is born a monstrous human–Xenomorph hybrid that kills her. The film thus continues the franchise's picture of a corporation that treats people as expendable in pursuit of biological weapons and enhancement. The science is fictional, though the idea of engineering humans for space echoes real speculation about adapting people to other worlds.

title: Altered
text: This science fiction action film, written and directed by Timo Vuorensola and starring Tom Felton, is set in an alternate present in which genetic enhancement has become the norm. People who cannot obtain or benefit from enhancements are marginalised and pushed into the underground. A few of them try to level the playing field for everyone, in a struggle in which, as the film's synopsis warns, every revolution has its cost. The cast also includes Liza Bugulova, Richard Brake and Igor Jijikine. The film was shot in Astana, Kazakhstan, premiered at the 2024 Cannes Film Festival and was released in Russia and the United States in 2025. The available sources give only this brief outline, so details of the story and its ending are not known. The premise is a society divided by genetic enhancement: the enhanced form the mainstream, and the unenhanced are pushed to the margins, an idea familiar from GATTACA. The story appears to follow those left behind as they fight for equality, which places genetic inequality and discrimination at the heart of the film. The only available source is a one-sentence synopsis, so it is not known what the enhancements consist of, who provides them, or how the film portrays the scientists or companies behind them. Real gene editing of human embryos for enhancement is banned or tightly restricted in most countries, and most traits people would want to enhance depend on many genes and on environment, but the film's worry about access and inequality echoes real ethical debates.

title: Bade Miyan Chote Miyan
text: A masked man attacks an Indian army convoy carrying a secret weapon. Captain Misha of Indian intelligence finds that the attacker's wounds heal instantly, and Colonel Azad has her recruit two court-martialled soldiers, Freddy and Rocky. With the hacker Pam they recover a stolen package from a London vault, which turns out to be Captain Priya Dixit, Freddy's former girlfriend, whose brain holds the codes of the Karan Kavach defence system. The masked man, who has shot Azad, kidnaps her and reveals himself as Kabir, a scientist the two soldiers believed they had killed seven years earlier. Kabir had proposed an army cloning programme, was ordered to shut it down as unethical and tried to sell it to India's enemies; the man Freddy and Rocky killed was his first clone, Eklavya. Kabir now commands regenerating clones of the two heroes and plans to disable Karan Kavach and launch airstrikes against Pakistan and China. The heroes destroy their clones and stop the strike, but Kabir survives. Cloning drives the plot. Kabir, a military scientist, created clones from the DNA of the soldiers Freddy and Rocky, programmed to obey orders and able to regenerate, intending them to fight wars without risking real soldiers' lives. When the army shut the programme down as unethical, he tried to sell it to India's enemies, faked his death with his first clone, Eklavya, whom he loved like a son, and later cloned Colonel Azad to take his place. The heroes end up fighting their own copies. The film presents Kabir as an amoral and vengeful villain and uses the army's ethical refusal as its line between legitimate and illegitimate science. Clones that are born as adults with programmed loyalty and the ability to heal fatal wounds belong to fantasy; real clones would be ordinary babies with no special powers.

title: Badland Hunters
text: In a post-apocalyptic Seoul laid waste by a deadly earthquake, set three years after Concrete Utopia, the hunter Nam-san scavenges to keep his village alive with his friend Choi Ji-wan. When Su-na, a girl from the village, is kidnapped, he traces her to an apartment complex controlled by Dr. Yang Gi-su, a rogue scientist who injects teenagers with a serum intended to make humans immortal, experiments that have killed many of them; his real aim is to revive his dead daughter, So-yeon. Joined by Lee Eun-ho, a sergeant from the camp who wants to free its prisoners, Nam-san and Ji-wan fight their way past Gi-su's mutant soldiers and rescue Su-na. Gi-su flees with his daughter's body in a suitcase, damages it while shooting at an angry mob, and is killed by Nam-san. The genetic element is limited. The villain, Dr. Yang Gi-su, conducts illegal experiments on teenagers with a serum meant to confer immortality (or, according to the Spanish Wikipedia, to create a new, more resistant race), and the experiments produce mutant soldiers who guard his camp. The sources do not describe the serum in genetic terms, and the mutants serve mainly as opponents in fights. Gi-su is a classic mad doctor driven by a private grief, the wish to bring back his dead daughter, whose experiments cost many young lives and who dies at the hands of the hero. The film is a star action vehicle in which science features only as the villain's tool.

title: Borderlands
text: On the planet Pandora, the mercenary Roland and the 'Psycho' Krieg abduct the teenager Tiny Tina from the facility where she was held. Elsewhere, the bounty hunter Lilith is hired by the corporate magnate and arms dealer Atlas to bring back his daughter Tina. Returning to Pandora, her home planet, for the first time since childhood, Lilith finds Tina with the help of the robot Claptrap, realises that Atlas wants her against her will and joins Roland, Krieg and Tina when Atlas's private army attacks. She learns that Tina was genetically engineered with material from the Eridians, the ancient race that once lived on Pandora, because Atlas believes only she can open the Vault that holds their technology. With Lilith's foster mother, Dr. Patricia Tannis, the group finds the key, but at the Vault Tina cannot open it; Lilith reveals that she herself is an Eridian, opens it and traps Atlas inside. Genetic engineering supplies the MacGuffin of this video-game adaptation. Tina has been genetically engineered with biological material from the Eridians, the vanished alien race of Pandora, because her 'father', the arms-dealing magnate Atlas, believes that only someone with Eridian biology can open the Vault and give him its advanced technology. The engineering is thus a corporate villain's tool for power, and Tina is its victim, hunted by his private army. The plan fails: the real key is Lilith, who turns out to be a full Eridian herself, and Atlas is trapped in the Vault. The film does not explain how the engineering was done and treats it as background to a comic action adventure, which critics widely panned. Mixing human and alien genetic material is pure science fiction.

title: Dune: Part Two
text: After the fall of House Atreides, Paul Atreides and his pregnant mother, Lady Jessica, a member of the Bene Gesserit sisterhood, take refuge with the Fremen of the desert planet Arrakis. Jessica becomes the tribe's Reverend Mother by drinking the poisonous Water of Life, which awakens the mind of her unborn daughter, Alia. Paul falls in love with the Fremen warrior Chani, who suspects the prophecy of a messiah is a Bene Gesserit myth, and leads raids on Harkonnen spice harvesting. The Bene Gesserit send Lady Margot Fenring to evaluate the Harkonnen heir Feyd-Rautha as a possible Kwisatz Haderach. Forced south, Paul drinks the Water of Life and gains prescience; he learns that Jessica is the daughter of Baron Harkonnen and that the Bene Gesserit arranged her union with Duke Leto to merge the two bloodlines. Proclaiming himself the messiah, Paul defeats the emperor's forces, kills Feyd-Rautha in a duel, claims the throne and launches a holy war. Like Frank Herbert's novel, the film presents the Bene Gesserit as a sisterhood running a centuries-long breeding programme, a form of eugenics aimed at producing the Kwisatz Haderach, a man with prescient powers. Part Two makes the programme more explicit than the 1984 film: Paul discovers that his mother is the Baron Harkonnen's daughter and that the sisterhood engineered the union of the Atreides and Harkonnen bloodlines, and the Bene Gesserit keep a back-up candidate in Feyd-Rautha, whom Margot Fenring is sent to assess. The programme is run not by scientists but by a religious and political order that manipulates genealogy and myth to gain power, and the film is critical of both. Paul's powers also depend on the spice and the Water of Life, not only on his ancestry. Planned breeding across many generations to produce a specific mental ability has no real-world equivalent, but it echoes historical eugenic projects of selective breeding in humans.

title: Golam
text: Isaac John, managing director of the company V-Tech, is found dead in a locked office restroom, apparently after slipping. ASP Sandeep suspects murder and questions the employees; Isaac's partner Gibson seems to have no motive, since Isaac's brother inherits the business. Sandeep finds that most employees were patients of Dr. Kuriakose, a neuropsychiatrist. Kuriakose had found DNA-altering mutagens in the blood of an employee, Meera, who had suffered an unexplained stillbirth, and in other staff with headaches and insomnia. Using files taken from Isaac's computer, he concludes that V-Pharma, a company Isaac co-founded, was testing an unfinished vaccine against a 'Human Mutagen Virus' on the employees through the office snacks and water, monitoring them with a DNA-sampling punch-card machine, and leaving them with permanent health problems. Sandeep works out that the employees jointly killed Isaac with carbon dioxide, but reports the death as accidental and turns to investigating V-Pharma's lab, while Gibson, also a biochemist involved in the scheme, takes over the company. This whodunnit hinges on illegal human experimentation by a pharmaceutical company. V-Pharma, co-founded by the murdered Isaac John, secretly tested a first-stage vaccine against a 'Human Mutagen Virus' (Red Virus) on the employees of its sister company, putting it into their food and water and sampling their DNA regularly through the office punch-card machine; the employees' blood contains mutagens capable of altering DNA, and they suffer a stillbirth, chronic symptoms and distress. The source says the aim was to create a supply and demand situation for the future vaccine. The scientist who uncovers the scheme, Dr. Kuriakose, is a sympathetic physician, while the company's leaders, Isaac and his biochemist partner Gibson, are presented as exploiters of their workers. The film takes the victims' side, as the investigating officer covers up their revenge killing.

title: Goodbye Earth
text: With 200 days left before an asteroid strikes the Earth, South Korea is under martial law; the rich have fled and those left behind face shortages, crime, suicides and scams. In the city of Woongcheon, the former teacher Jin Se-kyeong tries to protect children and discovers a trafficking ring run by escaped convicts, responsible for the deaths of many of her former students. Her fiancé, the geneticist Ha Yun-sang, returns from the United States to be with her. Army captain Kang In-a investigates the same convicts, and the assistant priest Woo Sung-jae takes charge of his parish when his superior disappears. The crime rings are linked to a cult-like elite raising money to escape abroad, which offers Yun-sang a place because of his research. The friends fail to secure seats for the children, and the elite's escape fails when one plane cannot land and the other crashes. As the end nears, the characters try to find peace, and Se-kyeong sets out with a gun to confront the traffickers. Genetics appears through one character. Ha Yun-sang is a geneticist at a biotechnology institute, and his research is considered important for humanity's survival after the asteroid impact, which is why the elitist group fleeing the country offers to take him, and Se-kyeong, along. He refuses to leave without her, and she will not abandon the children. The sources do not say what his research involves, and no genetic work is shown; in the end he devotes himself to documenting the city and its people for possible future visitors. His profession serves mainly to set up a moral choice between escape and loyalty.

title: Immaculate
text: Sister Cecilia, a young novice who believes God saved her life when she survived drowning as a child, is invited by Father Sal Tedeschi to join a convent in the Italian countryside that cares for dying nuns. Soon after taking her vows, she discovers that she is pregnant despite being a virgin, and the convent begins to venerate her as a new Virgin Mary. Her health deteriorates, a jealous nun tries to drown her, and her friend Sister Gwen, who protests, is mutilated and killed. Searching the convent at night, Cecilia finds her own file, which includes her karyotype. Tedeschi reveals that he was a geneticist before he became a priest, and that he has been using DNA taken from the convent's relic, a nail said to be from Christ's crucifixion, to impregnate nuns in the hope of bringing about a new messiah; earlier attempts produced malformed foetuses. Cecilia kills her captors, escapes and, after giving birth, destroys the baby. Genetics is the hidden mechanism behind the film's apparent miracle. Father Tedeschi, a geneticist turned priest, has been trying to create a clone or descendant of Jesus from DNA recovered from a relic, using nuns as unwilling surrogates. He is the religious version of the mad scientist, convinced of his mission and indifferent to the women he uses, with the backing of the convent's hierarchy. The film uses genetics to recast the Annunciation as reproductive coercion, linking the misuse of science to the control of women's bodies, and its final act turns on Cecilia's refusal to bear a child forced on her. The premise is far beyond real science: any DNA on a 2,000-year-old object would be degraded, fragmentary and almost certainly contaminated by later handling, and no technique could use such material to create a viable embryo.

title: In Vitro
text: In a future of food scarcity, Jack and Layla run an isolated cattle farm that produces meat by cloning. Jack keeps putting off Layla's visits to their son Toby at boarding school. One morning she is attacked by a clone of herself. Jack claims the clone was a test of human cloning meant as a source of income, that she was not supposed to wake and is dying of clone illness, and he tricks Layla into poisoning her. Layla sees through him and flees with the clone and the cattle driver Brady; Jack kills Brady and the clone dies leading Jack away. Layla learns that Toby left the school years ago and finds him, now a teenager, living with another Layla, who has divorced Jack and holds a restraining order. Back at the farm, Jack admits he replaced her because she was unhappy. Layla kills him and uses the cloning tank to make a new Toby. Human cloning drives this science-fiction thriller. On a farm that clones cattle for meat, Jack secretly grows copies of his wife: he presents the latest as an illegal money-making test, but finally admits that he replaces Layla whenever she is unhappy with him. The protagonist gradually discovers that she herself is a copy and that the original has escaped Jack, divorced him and is raising their son elsewhere. The clones suffer an unexplained "clone illness" and are treated as disposable, poisoned or abandoned when inconvenient. Jack is the film's villain, using the technology to control the women in his life, but the ending is bleak rather than liberating: after killing him, Layla uses the tank to make a clone of Toby to raise alone, continuing the cycle. Instantly grown adult clones are fiction; the film uses them to explore control and identity.

title: Jurassic World: Chaos Theory
themes: de extinction cloning animal experimentation bioweapon
text: Six years after Camp Cretaceous, with dinosaurs now loose on the mainland, the 'Nublar Six' reunite after their friend Brooklynn is apparently killed by an Allosaurus while investigating a conspiracy. Hunted by a silent woman known as the Handler and her trained Atrociraptors, they discover that Brooklynn had uncovered a global dinosaur-trafficking network involving corrupt officers of the Department of Prehistoric Wildlife. Stowing away on a smugglers' ship, they reach Senegal, where they find a secret dinosaur-cloning facility run by Dr. Sarr for 'the Broker', and learn that Brooklynn is alive and working undercover for the Broker to protect them. In Italy and Malta they confront the Broker, Soyona Santos, and investigate the genetics company Biosyn, while Brooklynn's double game strains their trust. In the final season they infiltrate Biosyn's facility in the Dolomites, run by Lewis Dodgson and Dr. Henry Wu, to rescue Ben's Ankylosaurus Bumpy and her young and expose the company's illegal experiments. Like the films it accompanies, the animated series is set in a world remade by de-extinction, and its villains are those who turn dinosaur cloning into business and weapons. Dr. Sarr runs a secret cloning facility in Senegal for the trafficker Soyona Santos, the Broker, who clones dinosaurs and weaponizes them for the black market; one of his creations is a blind, leucistic Baryonyx. Biosyn, under Lewis Dodgson and chief geneticist Dr. Henry Wu, conducts illegal experiments and trains Atrociraptors as weapons, and the heroes' final mission is to expose it and rescue the animals held there. The geneticists are uniformly villainous, serving profit and control, while the protagonists, a paleo-veterinarian and young people who love dinosaurs, side with the animals. Cloning extinct dinosaurs remains impossible because their DNA does not survive tens of millions of years, a point the franchise has long set aside.

title: Kingdom of the Planet of the Apes
text: About 300 years after the death of the ape leader Caesar, apes have formed many clans while most surviving humans have become feral and mute. Noa, a young chimpanzee of the falconry-practising Eagle Clan, returns from collecting eagle eggs to find his village burned by raiders led by the gorilla Sylva, his father killed and his clan abducted. On his way to rescue them he meets Raka, an orangutan scholar who teaches him Caesar's true legacy, and a human girl, whom Raka names Nova but who can speak and is called Mae. They are captured and taken to the coastal kingdom of Proximus Caesar, a tyrant who enslaves clans to open an old human vault full of technology. Mae wants a 'book' from the vault, in fact a satellite decryption key. Noa, his friends and Mae flood the vault and defeat Proximus, and Mae takes the key to a human settlement, which can now contact other survivors. Genetics lies in the background of this film, set three centuries after the events of the earlier Planet of the Apes films. The world it shows is the legacy of the ALZ-113 virus from those films, which in the series' backstory raised the apes' intelligence and in this film is said to have spread to the last immune humans and left most of humanity feral and speechless. The film does not show or discuss the scientists or the work behind the virus; its story concerns the apes' struggle over Caesar's legacy and Mae's attempt to restore human communication, and no genetic work is done on screen. The idea that a virus could make apes intelligent and strip humans of language is fiction.

title: Mobile Suit Gundam SEED Freedom
alt: 機動戦士ガンダムSEED FREEDOM
themes: genetic engineering human enhancement eugenics genetic discrimination
text: In this anime film, a sequel to the Gundam SEED series, the world peace organisation Compass, led by Lacus Clyne with Kira Yamato as its commander, fights the remnants of the anti-Coordinator terrorist group Blue Cosmos. The new Kingdom of Foundation, ruled by Queen Aura Maha Khyber and Prime Minister Orphee Lam Tao, proposes a joint operation but betrays Compass: its elite Black Knights telepathically manipulate Kira, nuclear missiles destroy Foundation's own capital to frame Eurasia, and Lacus is taken to Foundation's space base. Athrun Zala reveals that Aura, Orphee and Lacus belong to the Accords, a new race of enhanced Coordinators, and that Orphee and Lacus were genetically designed to rule mankind together under a version of the Destiny Plan, which assigns everyone a role according to their genes. Foundation destroys Moscow with the Requiem superweapon and demands that the world accept the plan. Lacus rejects Orphee, and Kira, Athrun and their allies defeat Foundation; Lacus and Kira choose each other over their designed destinies. Genetic engineering is at the heart of the Gundam SEED universe, built around genetically enhanced humans, the Coordinators, and the hostility of groups such as Blue Cosmos towards them. This film adds the Accords, a new race of enhanced Coordinators with high intelligence and telepathic powers that let them read and manipulate minds. They were created by Aura Maha Khyber, a former genetic researcher who became Foundation's queen, with Gilbert Durandal and Lacus's mother as co-researchers according to the Japanese source; Lacus and Orphee were designed as a pair destined to rule mankind. Foundation's aim is a version of the Destiny Plan, a eugenic social order in which genes decide each person's role and the Accords rule as a superior class, and it pursues it through deception, nuclear terror and mass murder. The heroes answer with freedom and love: Lacus, herself a product of the programme, refuses the destiny written in her genes. Telepathy cannot be engineered, but the film's warning about genetic determinism and designed elites is a classic theme.

title: Mother of the Bride
text: Emma Winslow, who works for the resort company Discovery in London, accepts her boyfriend RJ's proposal and tells her mother Lana, a geneticist who leads a medical research lab in San Francisco, that the wedding will take place in a month at a resort in Phuket, paid for by Discovery in exchange for publicity. In Thailand, Lana discovers that RJ's father is Will Jackson, the college boyfriend who disappeared from her life thirty years earlier, and fears RJ will hurt Emma the same way. Excluded from the planning by Discovery's brand manager, Lana clashes with Emma after a skinny-dipping escapade, while her best friend Janice sets her up with a doctor. Stranded with Will on a remote beach, Lana makes peace with him, then suspects him again after overhearing a call. After the wedding, Will explains the misunderstanding and proposes to her with the ring he bought decades ago. Genetics is incidental. The protagonist, Lana, is a geneticist who leads a medical research lab, but her profession plays no part in the story beyond characterising her as an accomplished scientist; the film is a romantic comedy about a destination wedding and an old romance rekindled.

title: Orphan Black: Echoes
text: Set in 2052, thirty-seven years after the events of Orphan Black, this spin-off follows Lucy, a woman who wakes up with no memory of who she is and has rebuilt a quiet life when her past catches up with her. She learns that she is a "printout", a human made with a printer developed by the scientist Kira Manning, daughter of the original series' heroine Sarah Manning, and funded by the billionaire Paul Darros. Kira created Lucy from an earlier body scan of her wife, Eleanor, after Eleanor lost her memory to Alzheimer's disease and died. Lucy also meets Jules, a teenage girl who looks exactly like her, printed by someone else. While Lucy searches for her identity with the help of her boyfriend Jack, Kira, who believed the printer destroyed, must confront what she has done and Darros's plans for the technology. The series updates the cloning theme of Orphan Black with a fictional technology: a machine that prints complete human bodies. In the backstory, Kira Manning's research on printing human DNA was meant to transform organ transplants, but she used it to recreate her dying wife, despite having opposed printing a whole person because of the history of human cloning. The series explores identity, memory and ownership: who a printed person is, whether she belongs to her creator, and what happens when a wealthy patron sees the technology as a source of power. The scientist is presented as brilliant and grieving, and the billionaire who funds her as the main threat, continuing the original's theme of corporate control over human bodies. Bioprinting of tissues is an active field of research, but printing a complete living human, let alone one with a predetermined body, is far beyond any real capability.

title: Project Silence
